latest.title: Normalizing sustainable fashion innovations: environmental messages and dynamic norms in circular fashion adoption
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether informational messages promote interest in fashion products made from agri-food waste and whether dynamic norm cues strengthen persuasion in a trend-sensitive, ambiguous market. Design/methodology/approach Overall, 183 Italian adults were randomly assigned to control, environmental message or environmental plus dynamic norm message conditions. Participants reported purchasing intention and willingness to pay a premium price. Pro-environmental self-identity and identification with sustainable fashion consumers were tested as moderators. Findings Only the combined environmental and dynamic norm message increased purchasing intention, whereas neither message affected willingness to pay, suggesting a distinction between motivational interest and financial commitment. Exploratory analyses suggested that the environmental message was more effective among participants with low identification with sustainable fashion consumers. Pro-environmental self-identity did not moderate message effects. Research limitations/implications Self-reported intentions and a highly educated Italian sample limit generalisability. Future studies should use behavioural measures, field experiments, longitudinal designs and diverse samples to test whether initial openness persists and translates into purchasing and price acceptance. Practical implications Environmental messages combined with dynamic norm cues can increase initial interest in agri-food waste fashion, but the promotional strategy did not increase willingness to pay, highlighting the importance of product, price and audience segmentation. latest.title: A EVOLUÇÃO TECNOLÓGICA E O NOVO COMPORTAMENTO DO CONSUMIDOR, QUE AGORA É MONITORADO POR ALGORITMOS
latest.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
latest.abstract: The expansion of digital platforms has transformed entertainment consumption, as algorithms recommend content based on user habits. This study aims to understand how these systems influence choices and behaviors, considering the effects of personalization and cultural diversity. The research draws upon the ideas of Marshall McLuhan, Theodor Adorno, Zygmunt Bauman, and Pierre Bourdieu. It notes that while platform recommendations facilitate access to content and help broaden exposure to different cultures, they also foster the creation of digital bubbles and the repetition of preferences. The study concludes that, despite their convenience, algorithms can steer consumer choices, underscoring the importance of maintaining a critical and conscious relationship with these platforms.

latest.title: The Role of Green Marketing of Electric Vehicles in Influencing Buying Intention in Indonesia
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of green marketing in influencing the buying intention of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), data from 330 respondents across Indonesia were collected via an online questionnaire to assess the relationship between the 4Ps of green marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Electric Vehicle Knowledge, and Environmental Attitude toward Green Buying Intention. The findings reveal that Green Product, Green Price, and Green Place have a significant and positive effect on EV buying intention, while Green Promotion and Electric Vehicle Knowledge did not show a statistically significant impact. Furthermore, although Environmental Attitude was found to have a strong direct influence on Green Buying Intention, it did not significantly moderate any of the tested relationships. The results imply that while Indonesians with strong environmental attitudes are more inclined to purchase EVs, promotional campaigns and general product knowledge from the 4Ps of green marketing may not yet be powerful enough to shift consumer behavior alone.

latest.title: U.S.-Canada Trade Tensions And Their Influence On Canadian Perception, National Sentiment And Consumer Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Business & Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study investigates how recent U.S. threatened and imposed tariffs under the Trump administration have influenced Canadian public sentiment and consumer behaviour. While traditional economic analysis of tariffs focuses on macro-level indicators such as GDP and trade balances, this research explores the sociopsychological and behavioural impacts of economic protectionism on individuals. Specifically, it examines the extent to which Canadian consumers’ awareness of tariffs correlates with negatives perceptions of Americans, increased nationalism, consumer ethnocentrism and retaliatory purchasing behaviour. Drawing upon theories such as social identity theory, consumer ethnocentrism and reactance theory, the study develops a conceptual framework linking tariff awareness to five key hypotheses. A cross-sectional, quantitative survey was conducted with 123 Canadian residents, collecting data on demographic variables, attitudes toward the U.S., national sentiments and purchasing patterns. The validated instruments consisted of both self-developed scales and pre-established scales including the CETSCALE (Shimp & Sharma, 1987) and Kosterman & Feshbach’s Nationalism scale (1989). Statistical analyses revealed significant relationships across several variables. Greater awareness of U.S. tariffs was associated with more negative perceptions of Americans, heightened national pride, a stronger preference for Canadian products and reduced support for U.S. brands. Notably, consumer behaviour in Canada has shifted, with increasing domestic product loyalty and signs of consumer boycott activity, evidenced by retail behaviour. latest.title: Toward a targeted localization framework: branding strategy replication in the Asia-Pacific bubble tea industry
latest.abstract: This study investigates how multinational corporations replicate branding strategies across culturally and institutionally diverse markets in the Asia-Pacific, specifically comparing Taiwan (a mature market) and Indonesia (an emerging market) via the bubble tea industry. Utilizing structural equation modeling (SEM) and multi-group analysis on 293 consumers with prior brand interaction, the research tests the sequential associations of brand equity components and the moderating role of national institutional maturity. The research confirms a consistent brand equity structural framework: Brand Image (BI) is positively associated with Brand Satisfaction (BS), which in turn correlates with Brand Trust (BT) and sequentially predicts Purchase Intention (PI). Furthermore, institutional contingencies moderate these pathways. In emerging markets with higher information asymmetry, purchase intention is heavily image-driven, relying on BI as a heuristic signal to mitigate risks. Conversely, mature markets are satisfaction-driven, emphasizing personal experiential validation over social signaling. This study introduces the Targeted Localization framework. While the strategic weights of brand image and satisfaction shift dramatically across contexts (supporting Targeted Localization), the empirical rejection of contextual differences in brand trust reveals its role as a universally critical baseline for transnational purchase intentions.

latest.title: The Hidden Economics of Digital Lending: Algorithmic Credit Intermediation, Consumer Choice and Regulatory Accountability under India’s Digital Lending Framework
latest.abstract: India’s 2025 digital-lending framework expressly addresses transparency in the presentation of loan offers. This article explores the transparency of digital marketplaces for loans. It relies on doctrinal, institutional economics and behavioral economics theories and concepts to substantiate its arguments. The article argues that, despite similarities in the wording of multiple loan offers, there may exist differences in the priorities and values of the offers, and borrowers may not be able to consider all those factors. The article considers the 2025 framework issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as a positive development to regulate lending marketplaces. However, the article identifies an imbalance where regulated entities remain responsible for LSP oversight, but verifying the operation of those controls may be difficult. The article describes a “price-choice-accountability” triad to illustrate that lending marketplaces should establish reasonable processes based on prior notice, and control misleading practices. The article does not examine the extent to which lending marketplaces, guided by the 2025 Directions, have introduced loan offer interfaces that bias against borrowers.

latest.title: Determinants of Green Purchase Intention and Green Purchase Behavior Among College Students in Fujian, China
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study addresses the limited evidence on factors influencing green purchase intention and green purchase behavior among college students in a regional vocational education context in China. Research design, data and methodology: A quantitative survey was conducted among 500 students from the Department of Automation Engineering at Meizhouwan Vocational Technology College. A non-probability sampling approach combining purposive, quota, and convenience sampling was adopted. A pilot test involving 30 participants was conducted, and content validity and reliability were assessed using the Item Objective Congruence method and Cronbach’s alpha. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling using AMOS were employed to evaluate the measurement model and test the hypothesized relationships. Results: Perceived behavioral control, subjective norms, attitude, environmental concern, and environmental knowledge significantly influenced green purchase intention (p < .05). Perceived behavioral control showed the strongest effect (β = 0.577), followed by subjective norms (β = 0.369). Green purchase intention significantly predicted green purchase behavior (β = 0.516). Conclusions: The findings demonstrate the importance of perceived behavioral control, social influence, and environmental awareness in strengthening green purchase intention, which subsequently promotes green purchase behavior. Universities and policymakers should implement targeted educational and campus-based initiatives to encourage sustainable consumption among students.

latest.title: Determinants of Customer Satisfaction and Repurchase Intention in Live Streaming Commerce: Evidence from Hangzhou, China
latest.abstract: Purpose: This article aims to examine the factors influencing customer satisfaction and repurchase intention toward live streaming commerce platforms among residents in Hangzhou, China. Research design, data and methodology: This study adopts a quantitative research design and collects data through an online questionnaire survey administered to 500 residents across four major urban districts of Hangzhou, China. A multi-stage non-probability sampling approach was employed, including judgmental sampling to select the study areas, quota sampling to determine the sample size, and convenience sampling for data collection. Structural equation modeling and confirmatory factor analysis were applied to examine the measurement and structural models. Model fit, construct reliability, and convergent and discriminant validity were rigorously assessed to ensure the robustness of the analytical results. Results: The empirical findings indicate that real-time interaction, flow, value, quality, and trust all have significant positive effects on customer satisfaction in live streaming commerce. Customer satisfaction, in turn, has a strong and significant influence on repurchase intention (β = 0.472). In addition, the five antecedent factors indirectly affect repurchase intention through customer satisfaction. Conclusions: All six proposed hypotheses were supported, confirming the achievement of the research objectives. The findings highlight customer satisfaction as a key mechanism linking platform-related and experiential factors to repurchase intention. Enhancing real-time interaction, immersive experiences, perceived value, service quality, and trust can effectively improve platform competitiveness in live streaming commerce.

latest.title: Building Trust: The Key to Purchase Intention Among Vocational College Students
latest.abstract: Purpose: Aims to identify the key role of building trust in live-streaming e-commerce scenarios, and to clarify the mechanism through which trust drives purchase intention among vocational college students. Specifically, an integrated conceptual framework is developed to examine the structural relationships among influencer characteristics, perceived value, trust, and behavioral intentions, thereby providing actionable implications for improving live-streaming sales effectiveness. Research Design, Data and Methodology: A quantitative survey (N = 500) was conducted among students from vocational colleges in Kaili, China, using purposive, quota, and convenience sampling. Confirmatory Factor Analysis was applied to assess measurement reliability and validity, and Structural Equation Modeling was employed to test hypothesized relationships and evaluate overall model fit. Results: The findings indicate that Popularity (β = 0.281), Professionalism (β = 0.368), Interactivity (β = 0.272), Perceived Usefulness (β = 0.294), and Price Discounts (β = 0.305) have significant positive influences on Trust. Meanwhile, Trust has a significant positive influence on purchase intentions (β = 0.620). Conclusions: This study reveals a mechanism of building trust to purchase intentions, extends trust-related theories. It contributes to the academic literature and provides practical guidance for influencers and platforms, empowering them to building trust and enhance conversion performance in competitive live streaming e-commerce environments.

latest.title: DINAMIKA PERILAKU KONSUMEN FASHION GENERASI Z : STUDI KOMPARATIF ANTARA FAST FASHION DAN BRAND LOKAL INDONESIA
latest.abstract: Transformasi digital dalam industri fashion turut mengubah pola konsumsi Generasi Z ketika menentukan pilihan antara fast fashion dan brand fashion lokal. Studi ini membandingkan preferensi terhadap kedua kategori tersebut sekaligus menganalisis peran Media Sosial dan Sustainability Awareness dalam Keputusan Pembelian Fashion. Sebanyak 320 responden Generasi Z berusia 17–27 tahun dilibatkan melalui purposive sampling. Data dianalisis dengan Paired Samples T-Test dan regresi linear berganda. Hasil analisis menemukan perbedaan preferensi yang signifikan (p = 0,022), dengan rata-rata brand lokal sebesar 17,69 dan fast fashion sebesar 16,36. Media Sosial dan Sustainability Awareness juga menunjukkan pengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Fashion, dengan kemampuan model menjelaskan 39% variasi keputusan pembelian. Temuan tersebut memperlihatkan bahwa pilihan fashion Generasi Z berkaitan dengan preferensi kategori produk, lingkungan digital, dan pertimbangan keberlanjutan.

latest.title: Closing the Knowledge Gap: How Moral Obligations, Perceived Benefits, and Dispositional Greed Shape Influencer Advertising Code Compliance
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of influencer marketing has outpaced regulatory enforcement and has increased the risk of noncompliance through misleading promotions and inadequate sponsorship disclosures. This study investigates whether and how enhancing influencers’ advertising code knowledge affects their intentions to comply with advertising regulations. Specifically, it examines whether increased knowledge enhances compliance intentions, whether this relationship is mediated by moral obligations and perceived benefits, and whether dispositional greed moderates these mediating pathways. Across four studies, involving 1,082 U.K.-based social media influencers, we employed diverse research designs. Study 1 uses a single-session pre–post design (N = 154); Study 2 adopts a two-wave pre–post design (N = 213); Study 3 applies a third-person, between-subjects design (N = 228); and Study 4 employs a randomized experimental design (N = 487). The findings reveal that greater advertising code knowledge significantly increases influencers’ intentions to comply. This effect is mediated by stronger moral obligations and heightened recognition of the compliance benefits. Furthermore, dispositional greed moderates the influence of knowledge on both moral obligations and perceived benefits. These findings highlight the importance of targeted education and training that build influencers’ advertising code knowledge as a lever for strengthening ethical conduct and regulatory compliance.

latest.title: Sustainable talent attraction in hospitality: configurational pathways to Generation Z career intention
latest.abstract: Sustainable hospitality requires young people to perceive hospitality work as a viable, responsible, and socially acceptable long-term career. Building a responsible employer value proposition (EVP) is central to sustainable talent attraction, yet prior research largely treats employer attributes as independent, linear predictors. This study adopts a configurational approach to examine how sustainable EVP signals shape Generation Z hospitality career intention in Thailand. Data from 180 hospitality students and recent graduates were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA). Financial rewards, flexibility, and ethical commitment were combined into an exploratory higher-order construct, Core Employer Value (CEV), representing a bundled baseline of responsible employment. PLS-SEM identified career feasibility as the sole significant predictor. fsQCA converged on this: career feasibility appeared in every pathway to high intention but was never sufficient alone, always requiring two of the remaining mutually substitutable conditions (CEV, well-being support, or social endorsement). Conversely, low intention followed an asymmetric ‘dealbreaker’ logic driven by absent career feasibility despite other positive signals. This exploratory study extends signalling theory toward composite signal bundles, demonstrates the value of pairing symmetric and asymmetric methods, and reframes these attributes as social sustainability indicators.

latest.title: Social Media Influencers in Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Communication: A Hybrid Bibliometric and Thematic Review
latest.abstract: Addressing global sustainability challenges and advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 12 and SDG 13, requires communication that can support pro‐environmental behaviour and responsible consumption. Social media influencers (SMIs) increasingly mediate such communication by translating CSR and sustainability issues into messages linked to everyday practices. This study conducts a hybrid bibliometric and systematic thematic review following the SPAR‐4‐SLR protocol. The bibliometric corpus comprised 206 peer‐reviewed journal articles and reviews indexed in Scopus and Web of Science. Six citation communities comprising 129 documents were retained for interpretation of the citation network, while 86 studies were selected for full‐text thematic synthesis. Performance analysis and science mapping using Bibliometrix (R), VOSviewer, and Gephi were integrated with full‐text thematic synthesis. The review identifies three themes, namely influencer‐driven sustainable communication from a communication perspective, influencer‐driven sustainable consumption from a marketing perspective, and influencer‐driven CSR communication. Across these themes, source credibility, authenticity, congruence, and parasocial relationships form recurring persuasion mechanisms, while the salience and involvement of the organisation vary. The evidence base is concentrated on environmental issues, responsible consumption, and short‐term audience outcomes, with less attention to social equity, economic and legal CSR responsibilities, and verifiable sustainability outcomes. latest.title: TOUTING THE AMERICAN DREAM TO MOVE PROSPECTS DOWN THE PATH TO PURCHASE USING A CONCEPTUAL DECISION-MAKING FRAMEWORK
latest.venue: DigitalCommons - Kennesaw State University (Kennesaw State University)
latest.abstract: The American dream is a concept that is echoed across our society, and while the data shows Americans do not overwhelmingly believe in the dream, marketers continue to include it and the issue of economic prosperity in their agendas.Through a novel framework that overlaps a deeply studied mass communication theory with a decision-making framework used in marketing, this paper explores a new lens to understand how marketers identify strategies and tactics, build agendas, and make sales by touting the American dream.These concepts are important to understand because of the power and influence each has, which, as separate entities are powerful enough, but together, can create an environment that is powerfully persuasive.The conceptual model presented in this paper helps to visualize these interconnected processes in a way that has not been done before in today's modern media landscape.This model is an important visualization of the power marketers have when they build strategies and plan tactics to move an individual down the path of purchase. Keywords -American dream,

latest.title: IMPACT OF SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING ON YOUTH BUYING PATTERN
latest.abstract: The study examines the impact of social media marketing on the buying pattern of youth. It focuses on the influence of social media advertisements, influencer promotions, online reviews, platform preferences and impulsive buying behaviour. The study adopts a descriptive and empirical research design and uses primary data collected through a structured questionnaire. The project reports responses from 115 respondents and applies percentage analysis, tabulation and graphical presentation to interpret the data. The findings indicate that social media is an important source of product information for young consumers. Instagram is reported as the most-used platform, while reviews, offers, influencer content and short videos are among the factors shaping purchase decisions. The study also identifies fake advertisements and product-quality concerns as important problems. The results highlight the need for transparent digital promotions and informed consumer decision-making.

latest.title: Line curvilinearity–masculinity associations on packaging influence expected taste intensity of green tea
latest.abstract: Visual cues on product packaging play an important role in shaping consumers’ sensory expectations before they consume. Although line curvilinearity is commonly used in green tea packaging, little research has examined how angular versus rounded lines influence expected taste intensity or the psychological mechanisms. This research aims to examine how line curvilinearity ​(Angular vs. Rounded) affects expected taste intensity in green tea packaging. It also investigates the roles of perceived femininity and masculinity in this relationship. Three online experiments were conducted with 458 participants recruited through the Credamo platform in China. Participants viewed green tea packaging featuring angular or rounded lines and rated expected taste intensity, perceived masculinity and femininity, and willingness to purchase. Across three studies, angular lines (vs. rounded lines) were associated with higher expected taste intensity. They were also associated with higher perceived masculinity ( B = 1.66, p < .001 in S1; B = 2.21, p < .001 in S2; B = 1.76, p < .001 in S3) and lower perceived femininity ( B = -1.32, p < .001 in S1; B = -1.72, p < .001 in S2; B = -1.25, p < .001 in S3). Perceived masculinity consistently accounted statistically for the relationship between line curvilinearity and expected taste intensity, whereas perceived femininity did not. Expected taste intensity was also positively associated with willingness to purchase. This research offers insights into how tea enterprises can optimize their packaging design. This research examines how a common design element in green tea packaging (Angular vs. Rounded lines) influences consumers’ expected taste intensity and highlights the unique mediating role of perceived masculinity.

latest.title: Building Customer Loyality for Marning Corn in Bulukumba: The Impact of Brand Image, Service Quality, and Product Quality on Purchase Decisions and Customer Satisfaction
latest.venue: Journal of Global Innovations in Agricultural Sciences
latest.abstract: Marning corn products, typical food, and souvenirs from the Bulukumba district are packaged simply without complete product information. Yet by integrating well-designed packaging with clear and relevant product information that can improve product quality, brands can improve the overall consumer experience, build trust, and foster long-term loyalty. This research aims to analyze the direct and indirect influence of brand image, service quality, and product quality on purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction on consumer loyalty to making corn. The research method used quantitative analysis with structured interview techniques using a sample of corn buyers in Bulukumba Regency. The data analysis used is structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis using the AMOS application. The research results show that consumer satisfaction and brand image have a significant direct influence on loyalty. Brand image and service quality have an impact on purchasing decisions. Product quality, service quality, and brand image influence consumer satisfaction. Meanwhile, the variables of service quality and production quality do not have a significant effect on consumer loyalty through purchasing decisions and consumer satisfaction as intervening variables of brand image, service quality, and production quality. Increasing income in the Morning Corn business can be achieved by prioritizing brand image, service quality, and product quality so that later it can increase the number of buyers and increase consumer loyalty. Keywords: Customer loyalty, buying decision, customer satisfaction, brand image, service quality, product quality and marning corn.

latest.title: Coping with sustainability information overload: The role of generative artificial intelligence literacy
latest.venue: Ho Chi Minh City Open University Journal of Science- Economics and Business Administration
latest.abstract: Consumers can use sustainability information to consume responsibly; however, excessive and complex sustainability claims might confuse consumers and hinder proper evaluations. Based on cognitive appraisal theory, this study empirically investigates the impacts of sustainability information overload (SIO) on green information avoidance (GIA) and green information verification behavior (GIVB) and examines the moderating role of generative AI literacy (GAIL) and the associations of GIA and GIVB with green purchase decision confidence (GPDC). Data from an online cross-sectional survey of 468 adult consumers in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings revealed that SIO positively influenced GIA, and GIA negatively influenced GPDC. However, SIO did not negatively influence GIVB on average. GAIL significantly moderated the SIO-GIVB relationship: SIO was negatively associated with GIVB at low GAIL but not significantly at mean or high GAIL.GIVB positively influenced GPDC. An indirect effect of SIO on GPDC through GIA is significant, but the indirect effect through GIVB is not significant unconditionally. These results suggest that sustainability information overload is associated with distinct coping responses. From a practical perspective, sustainability portals and shopping applications involving GenAI should emphasize evaluability and verifiability rather than enhancing disclosures. Through defining GAIL as a digitally mediated capability from the consumer’s perspective which can serve as a coping tool, this paper builds on cognitive appraisal theory in the context of AI-mediated sustainable consumption and explains the critical engagement of consumers with sustainability information amid overload situations

latest.title: The impact of environmental knowledge on water waste in restaurants on complaining behavior intention: The mediating role of perceived motivation and skepticism
latest.venue: Journal of Tourism Leisure and Hospitality
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of environmental knowledge about water waste in restaurants on consumers' intentions to complain, while also elucidating the mediating roles of perceived motivation and skepticism in this relationship. A scenario-based experimental research design was employed, and data were gathered from 388 restaurant goers through an online survey. Participants were randomly assigned to two restaurant scenarios: one in which water-saving practices were not observable and another in which they were prominently displayed. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling and bootstrapped mediation analyses in SPSS 26 and AMOS 23. The research findings demonstrate that, in the first scenario—characterized by the absence of visible communication about water conservation—environmental knowledge had no direct, significant influence on the intention to display complaint behavior. Environmental knowledge increased perceived motivation and skepticism. Perceived motivation did not directly and significantly influence the intention to engage in complaint behavior; however, skepticism increased the intention to engage in such behavior. In the second scenario, where water-saving methods were visible, environmental knowledge directly and positively affected the intention to complain, perceived motivation, and skepticism; furthermore, perceived motivation and skepticism partially mediated the relationship between environmental knowledge and the intention to complain. The findings suggest that restaurants must not only implement eco-friendly practices but also communicate them to consumers in a transparent, visible, and trustworthy way. latest.title: Youth engagement with algorithmic consumerism cultures: A systematic psychological review.
latest.abstract: This article presents a systematic literature review and a conceptual framework for understanding how youth engage with and are influenced by algorithmic consumerism cultures on social media. We integrate findings from 72 quantitative , experimental, and qualitative psychological studies to examine a relatively new form of consumer culture that has been advanced by social media and algorithmic technologies, in which novel marketing methods and the strategic targeting of youth through social media influencers are increasingly prevalent. We conceptualize this as algorithmic consumerism cultures that are unique in their pace, individualization , user engagement, and implicitness. The results show that youth engagement with consumerism online is shaped by three main psychological processes: intrapersonal processes influencing identity and well-being , social processes influencing motivation and persuasion , and cognitive and moral developmental processes influencing critical engagement and advertising literacy . Advancing this field requires methodologies that capture the reciprocal influence between algorithm-driven consumerist content on social media and youth’s active navigation of this content. This requires conceptualizing such spaces as subcultures with their own norms and practices that need to be investigated through the perspectives of the “ natives ” of those cultures: youth.

latest.title: A Study on Lead Management and Customer Engagement Practices in the Residential Real Estate Sector
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Residential real estate is a high-involvement purchase in which customers generally compare several projects, evaluate affordability and consult family members before making a decision. For a channel partner, the quality of lead management and customer engagement therefore plays an important role in moving an enquiry towards a site visit and, ultimately, a booking. This paper examines the lead management and customer engagement practices observed at Thee House Of Real Estate Solutions Pvt. Ltd., Pune, during the internship undertaken by Om Sunil Tiwari. The study follows a descriptive and exploratory approach. Primary information was drawn from participant observation, customer requirement calls, follow-up activities, property presentations, virtual interactions, site-visit coordination and discussions with the sales team. Secondary information was drawn from project brochures, available sales material and relevant concepts of customer relationship management, relationship marketing and consumer buying behaviour. The analysis is qualitative because detailed company-wide conversion statistics and complete commercial records were not available. The observations indicate that lead conversion is influenced by the quality of the initial enquiry, accurate understanding of customer requirements, clarity of pricing and project information, timely follow-up, product knowledge and coordination for site visits. Customers evaluate properties on factors such as budget, location, configuration, purchase purpose, possession expectations and developer credibility. The paper recommends structured lead qualification, updated customer records, planned follow-up, personalised communication and verified property information. latest.title: From sustainability practices to consumer behaviour: a PLS-SEM analysis of sustainable packaging adoption in the FMCG food sector
latest.abstract: Growing environmental concerns and plastic waste are driving the need for sustainable packaging solutions for the FMCG food sector. Understanding consumer attitude and purchasing behavior for sustainably packaged food products is crucial for promoting sustainable practices. This study assesses the association between the 5R's sustainability practices, consumer attitude, purchase intention, and actual purchasing behavior towards sustainably packaged FMCG food products. Primary data were collected from 210 consumers using the purposive sampling method from various hypermarkets in Coimbatore city. The data were analysed by Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling with SmartPLS 4 software. From the results, it is revealed that 5R sustainability practices significantly influence consumer attitude (β = 0.730) towards sustainably packaged food products. Furthermore, consumer attitude has a positive influence on purchase intention (β = 0.666), whereas purchase intention considerably influences actual purchasing behavior (β = 0.543). However, the direct association between attitude and actual purchasing behavior was not significant (β = −0.115), indicating the existence of an intention–behavior gap in sustainable consumption. The structural model explains 53.3% of the variance in attitude, 44.4% in purchase intention, and 22.5% in actual purchasing behavior, highlighting that purchase intention acts as a key mediating factor between attitude and actual behavior. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening consumer intention and improving the availability of sustainably packaged food products to enhance actual purchasing behaviour

latest.title: Product Packaging Design and Buying Behavior of Shoe Retail Consumers
latest.venue: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
latest.abstract: Product packaging design is an important element of product presentation that may influence consumers’ perceptions and purchasing decisions. However, limited research has examined the relationship between product packaging design and buying behavior among shoe retail consumers in the Philippine retail context, particularly in Davao City. This study examined the level of product packaging design and buying behavior among shoe retail consumers, determined whether significant differences existed in these variables when grouped according to monthly income, and assessed the relationship between product packaging design and buying behavior. A quantitative, non-experimental, descriptive-correlational-comparative research design was employed. The study involved 200 shoe retail consumers selected through convenience-quota sampling, with 50 participants assigned to each of four monthly income groups. Data were collected using a validated structured questionnaire and analyzed using mean, standard deviation, analysis of variance, and Pearson correlation. Results showed that product packaging design was at a very high level (m=3.71), while buying behavior was likewise at a very high level (m=3.70). No significant difference was found in product packaging design across income groups (p=.150). Similarly, buying behavior did not significantly differ across income groups (p=.075). However, a strong positive and statistically significant relationship was found between product packaging design and buying behavior, with a correlation coefficient of r=.822 and a probability value of p<.001. The findings indicate that consumers generally perceive shoe packaging favorably and demonstrate strong buying behavior regardless of income group. latest.title: Consumer Purchase Intention Differences Between AI Streamers and Human Streamers in Live-streaming E-commerce
latest.venue: Asia Pacific Economic and Management Review
latest.abstract: This study employs the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework and social presence theory to investigate the relation of host type to social presence, host trust, and consumers’ purchase intention. It treats host type as the external stimulus (S), social presence and host trust as the internal psychological response (O), and purchase intention as the behavioral response (R) of the model. It puts forward a sequential pathway that host type may be in a way to shape the perceived social presence and, through host trust, purchase intention. We use video clips of live-streaming e-commerce session as the stimuli in a single-factor, randomized between-subjects experiment. 157 participants were randomly assigned to watch a product promotion video with either AI host or a human host. They completed a questionnaire of social presence, host trust and purchase intention. Independent-samples t-tests, regression analysis, and Bootstrap-based sequential mediation analysis are used to see the differences between host types and the psychological mechanism that may explain the differences.

latest.title: Factors Influencing Beverage Purchase Decisions Among Physically Active Individuals: A Cross-Sectional Survey
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science Research and Review
latest.abstract: Sports and functional beverages are no longer bought only by competitive athletes, yet little is known about what shapes the choices of ordinary active consumers. This study examined how brand, nutritional information, price and packaging influence beverage purchases among physically active people aged 15 to 35. A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 103 respondents using purposive sampling method, conducted from June 2026 to August 2026. Differences by gender, age group, primary activity (gym, running, sport) and weekly training frequency were examined using Descriptive statistics, t-test, ANOVA, Tukey HSD Post Hoc. Nutritional information (M = 4.09) and price (M = 3.85) were rated as more important than brand (M = 3.49) and packaging (M = 3.32). Women reported more favourable packaging attitudes than men (p = .048, d = 0.44). Runners reported higher price sensitivity (p = .010, Tukey-adjusted) and gave price greater importance (p = .029) than team and racquet sport participants. No significant differences were found by age group, training frequency or purchase frequency. Beverage firms can utilize these findings in order to market to their target consumer base more effectively, which will allow them to achieve greater sales and revenue.

latest.title: Branding visual en la era algorítmica: Autenticidad, participación humana y modelos híbridos
latest.venue: VISUAL REVIEW International Visual Culture Review / Revista Internacional de Cultura Visual
latest.abstract: Este estudio examina cómo la inteligencia artificial generativa transforma la identidad visual de marca y la percepción del consumidor. Mediante un análisis teórico integrado con estudios de caso específicos, se evidencia que el contenido generado por IA activa respuestas ambivalentes: mientras la personalización y eficiencia potencian el engagement, la ausencia de señales humanas erosiona la autenticidad percibida. Los hallazgos revelan que los modelos híbridos humano-IA preservan la confianza cuando la coherencia con la autoimagen del consumidor compensa la automatización. Se identifican desafíos éticos: sesgos culturales, propiedad intelectual y transparencia, demandando marcos normativos internacionales para una adopción de IAG en branding.

latest.title: Effect of Augmented Reality Marketing Strategies on Consumer Brand Performance of Hotels in South-South Nigeria
latest.venue: British Journal of Management and Marketing Studies
latest.abstract: The study examined the effect of augmented reality marketing strategies on consumer brand performance, using a case study of hotels in South-South Nigeria. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from customers of hotels in Edo and Delta States, targeting a population of 312 regular guests. Using Taro Yamane's formula, a sample size of 175 was determined, and purposive sampling was employed to select respondents with AR marketing experience. A structured questionnaire was used as the research instrument. Reliability was confirmed using the test-retest reliability method. Data analysis utilized descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings revealed that interactive product demonstration (ß = 0.330, P < 0.05), virtual product placement (ß = 0.406, P < 0.05), and telepresence (ß = 0.166, P < 0.05) positively affect customer brand performance. The study concludes that augmented reality marketing strategies significantly enhance consumer brand performance in the hospitality industry. These strategies create immersive and engaging experiences that allow customers to interact with hotel offerings in a more personalized and meaningful way. The study recommended that hotels should integrate telepresence features, such as virtual tours and live customer interactions, to create a sense of connection and accessibility, further strengthening customer engagement and satisfaction.

latest.title: From Reach to Awareness: Online Brand Awareness of a Niche Hungarian Skincare Brand – The Case of Elyn’s Lab
latest.abstract: Introduction: A large online reach does not automatically become brand awareness, which is a particular problem for niche brands competing with established ones. Elyn’s Lab, a young Hungarian manufacturer of active-ingredient skincare, illustrates this: a TikTok video of the brand was seen 5.2 million times, yet few consumers know the brand. Aim: The aim of this paper is to examine why reach does not become awareness for a niche skincare brand and to derive from the literature and the data an online campaign design that can be evaluated. Materials and Methods: An exploratory single-case study combined an online questionnaire (N = 31, convenience sample, January–February 2026) with secondary data on the retail turnover of cosmetics and toiletries in Hungary (2006–2025), deflated with the price index of personal care products. Awareness was estimated with Wilson confidence intervals; trend and seasonality were estimated from real values. SWOT, Porter’s five forces, and PESTEL were used as contextual tools. Results: Aided awareness was 12.9% (4 of 31; 95% CI 5.1–28.9%), and price and customer reviews were the most important choice factors. Real turnover grew by 3.4% per year in 2006–2025 but only by 1.7% per year in 2019–2025, and most of the nominal growth in 2022–2023 reflected higher prices. Sales peak in the fourth quarter (seasonal index 1.15). Three propositions (reach is not sufficient for awareness; educational content from credible sources supports awareness; reviews and an incentive support the first purchase) are the basis of an ex ante campaign design with indicators and a sample-size-based evaluation plan. Conclusion: Niche brands should aim at relevant, memorable, and credible exposure of the primary target group rather than at reach alone. The propositions a

latest.title: Business Development, Sales and Marketing Practices in Real Estate: A Descriptive Case Study of Blisss Red PVT. LTD.
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Real estate is a high-involvement service category in which customers commonly evaluate substantial financial commitments, location, property suitability, documentation, trust and long-term value before making a purchase decision. Sales and marketing activities in this sector therefore extend beyond promotion: they include identifying potential buyers, understanding requirements, communicating property information, coordinating site visits, supporting comparisons and maintaining client relationships. This paper examines business development, sales and marketing practices in the context of Blisss Red Pvt. Ltd., a Pune-based real estate channel partner and sales-services organisation dealing with apartments, plots and commercial property. The study is developed from the organisation and project details in the On-the-Job Training (OJT) Initial Information Report for the period 15 May to 15 August 2026, stated as 92 days. A descriptive case-study approach is adopted, following the structure of an existing MBA research paper while adapting the subject to real estate client advisory. The analysis uses documentary information and established marketing concepts to organise the business-development process into lead identification, qualification, needs assessment, property matching, client communication, site-visit coordination, follow-up and relationship management. The available source does not provide a customer sample, transaction records, conversion rates or a verified performance dataset; consequently, the paper does not claim measured sales growth or statistically significant effects. It proposes a practical framework for lead tracking, transparent communication, customer segmentation and performance measurement that may help a real estate channel partner improve process

latest.title: Internalization of Halal Lifestyle Values in The Use of Syass Glow Body Lotion Among Young Muslim Women in Pinrang
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Law and Humanities
latest.abstract: Background/Introduction: The growing awareness of Islamic values highlights the importance of halal lifestyles in cosmetic consumption, particularly among young Muslim women influenced by beauty standards, social environments, and digital marketing. Research Objectives: This study examines the understanding and internalization of halal lifestyle values and their influence on the consumption of Syass Glow body lotion among young Muslim women in Tadokkong, Pinrang. Methodology: Using a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation. Data analysis involved reduction, display, and conclusion drawing, guided by halal lifestyle, Maqashid al-Shariah, and consumer decision-making theories. Results: The findings indicate that participants have a basic understanding of halal lifestyles, which is not consistently reflected in their consumption practices. Social media and peer influence play a greater role in shaping consumption behavior than religious and family education. From a Maqashid al-Shariah perspective, these practices do not fully reflect the preservation of religion (hifz al-din), life (hifz al-nafs), intellect (hifz al-'aql), and wealth (hifz al-mal). Purchasing decisions are primarily driven by the desire for brighter skin, affordability, peer recommendations, and social media promotions rather than halal considerations. Unique Contribution: This study reveals a gap between understanding of the halal lifestyle and actual cosmetic consumption practices, contributing empirical insights into Islamic consumer behavior from a Maqashid al-Shariah perspective. Conclusion: It highlights the need to strengthen halal literacy and consumer awareness through religious education and consumer protection initiatives.

latest.title: Green Human Resource Management and Environmental Performance in Tanzanian Local Government Authorities: The Role of Green Organizational Culture and Organizational Citizenship Behaviour towards Environment
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
latest.abstract: This study investigated the effect of Green Human Resource Management on Environmental Performance in Tanzanian Local Government Authorities (LGAs) with a focus on the mediating effect of Green Organisational Culture and the moderating effect of Organisational Citizenship Behaviour toward Environment.A quantitative research design was adopted, and the study was conducted among employees of Tanzanian LGAs.Respondents were selected using stratified and simple random sampling techniques.A total of 400 questionnaires were given out, 231(57.8%) of which were completed and used for analysis.Data were analysed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), using Smart-PLS 4. Findings showed that Green Human Resource Management had a positive effect on Environmental Performance.Furthermore, the findings show that the relationship between Green Human Resource Management and Environmental Performance is positively and significantly mediated by Green Organisational Culture.This implies that a green organisational culture enhances the effect of Green Human Resource Management on environmental performance.The findings also showed that Organisational Citizenship Behaviour toward Environment positively and significantly moderates the relationship between Green Human Resource Management and Environmental Performance, meaning that the positive effect of Green Human Resource Management on environmental performance is stronger when employees engage in higher levels of voluntary environmental behaviour.The study recommends LGAs to improve Green Human Resource Management functions for better environmental performance.LGAs should also improve green organisational culture and promote environmental citizenship behaviour of employees to maximise the environmental benefits a

latest.title: The Algorithmic Consumer: A Theoretical Perspective on Consumer Buying Behavior in Intelligent Markets
latest.abstract: Today, businesses are making more and more use of Artificial Intelligent (AI) technologies in their operations. This widespread use of AI technologies is changing how a consumer searches, evaluates and purchases products in the online intelligent markets. Consumer behavior is shaped by consumer’s own cognition as well as influence by machine learning systems (AI technologies). These advanced systems use algorithmic personalization, predictive analysis, ranking systems and automated decision support to guide the consumers. To understand the consumer buying behavior in these intelligent markets, this paper, titled “The Algorithmic Consumer: A Theoretical Perspective on Consumer Buying Behavior in Intelligent Markets,” proposes an integrated conceptual framework. “Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) (Venkatesh et al. 2003)”, “Diffusion of Innovations (Rogers, 2003)” and “Disruptive Innovation Perspectives (Christensen, 1997)” are the foundations of this research. This paper argues that the algorithmic influence works through three interconnected mechanisms namely, behavioral reinforcement through personalization, cognitive effort reduction and perceived performance enhancement. Here, conventional consumer behavior models are extended by adding new constructs such as algorithmic trust, perceived AI transparency, adaptive habit formation and data-driven social influence. This paper proposes that AI tools and systems do not simply play the role of marketing tools but also actively influence consumer preferences, attention, post-purchase learning and habits. In this work, theory is being built methodologically and conceptual synthesis technique is used. Model abstraction (simplification) and comparison analysis is used to achieve proposed conceptual inte

latest.title: From Shelf to Sale: Customer Engagement, In-Store Promotion and Merchandising Execution in Indian Processed-Food FMCG Retail
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: This study looks at how three point-of-sale levers work together in Indian packaged-food FMCG retail: promoter-led customer engagement, sampling-based promotion and shelf merchandising. Design/methodology/approach – The work is an embedded participant-observation case study drawn from a two-month on-the-job placement as a brand promoter for a Pune-based food manufacturer. All observations were made in one modern-trade store in Jalgaon, Maharashtra. Structured field records were examined descriptively and covered five promotion days (500 shoppers approached), one peak sales day (134 units across four stock-keeping units), five shelf audits and a log of shopper questions. Findings – Pooled across the promotion days, 65.0% of approached shoppers heard a product explanation, 41.2% agreed to taste or try the product, and 25.6 units were sold per 100 shoppers approached. Among shoppers who received an explanation, the share who went on to trial barely moved (62.5–65.5%), whereas sales yield ranged from 18.7% to 33.6% and followed how many shoppers the promoter managed to draw into conversation. On the peak day, cheaper SKUs delivered most of the units while expensive SKUs delivered most of the revenue. Shortfalls in eye-level placement, cleanliness and stock appeared together in the same two audits. Shopper questions grouped around how to use a product, whether a pack is good value, whether the ingredients can be trusted and what the product will taste like. Originality/value – The paper documents a transparent, repeatable field protocol and proposes five propositions about the engagement-to-purchase funnel for a mid-sized regional brand, a context that retail-marketing research seldom covers. Limitations – The evidence comes from a single outlet and five promotion days witho

latest.title: Brand recommendations by generative AI chatbots: A comparative analysis in consumer decision-making
latest.abstract: This study explored the algorithmic gatekeeping role of generative AI chatbots in consumer decision-making. Using algorithmic content analysis and an audit design, it examined the brand recommendations of the three most widely used chatbots in Türkiye: ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. Four product categories were selected by crossing involvement level and consumption motivation: detergent, chocolate, smartphone and an international holiday. Each prompt was submitted once to each model in a neutral and an emotional version, and the resulting 24 responses were coded descriptively. Neutral prompts mostly elicited technical and functional arguments, whereas emotional wording shifted the persuasion frame toward emotional appeals in 8 of 12 responses; predominantly emotional responses appeared only in hedonic categories. In the holiday category, all three models framed even the neutral prompt in romantic terms. The models typically offered three to ten brands rather than a single one, yet ChatGPT stated a first-person preference in every response and displayed priced shopping cards in five of eight. The findings suggest that generative AI can act as an intermediary that shapes brand visibility and has the potential to steer consumer preferences, raising questions for marketing ethics and large language model optimization.

latest.title: How do Islamic economics and finance academics perceive consumer boycotts?
latest.abstract: Globalization and intensifying competition necessitate that companies in international markets better understand consumers to ensure sustainability. Consequently, consumer boycotts, reflecting mass reactions, are rapidly proliferating due to diverse motivations and potential effects. This study aims to examine the perspectives of Turkish academics specializing in Islamic economics and finance on consumer boycotts, specifically exploring the link between these boycotts and religious motivations. While consumer boycotts are a documented area of study, this research offers a novel contribution by investigating the issue from the viewpoint of Islamic economics and finance academics, who engage with the topic both theoretically and practically. The research utilized a qualitative methodology, conducting semi-structured interviews with 12 academics in the field. Data were analyzed thematically and coded into specific main themes and sub-themes with the help of the Atlas.ti qualitative data analysis software. By examining the evaluations of domain experts rather than general consumer cohorts, this study fills a significant gap in the existing literature and extends prior research on religious political consumerism. Findings indicate that academics perceive boycotts as a manifestation of individual and social consciousness, with religious sensitivities partially influencing boycott decisions. Political, ethical, and economic factors also support this stance. However, for the non-Muslim community, humanitarian and moral considerations emerged as the strongest motivators. The study also highlights the importance of developing and disseminating alternative products to sustain boycotts.

latest.title: Sustainability Orientation in New Product Development for High‐Involvement Business‐to‐Business Innovations
latest.abstract: Adapting to climate change has led to innovative sustainable products, yet their market adoption remains uncertain. This underscores the need to explore the link between companies' new product development and their customers' orientation to sustainability in a B2B context. To address this, we developed a path model examining winemakers' willingness to adopt a microtechnology‐based crop‐protection product to mitigate the effects of climate change. A survey of 78 German winemakers, analyzed by partial least squares structural equation modeling, revealed a positive link between sustainable product‐feature orientation and willingness to use, mediated by trust in science and product interest. Sustainable product‐feature orientation showed a negative relationship with trust in science and willingness to use, while trust in science positively influenced product interest and adoption willingness. Our study uniquely connects approaches to new product development with novel technology and high‐involvement products for small and medium‐sized enterprises in the agricultural sector.

latest.title: The Art of Resourcefulness: Decoding Jugaad in Bottom of the Pyramid Consumer Behavior
latest.abstract: This pioneering study investigates what drives Bottom of the Pyramid (BOP) consumers to adopt jugaad , a resource‐constrained workaround practice conceptualized here as a form of adaptive consumption that sustains the circular economy, through the lenses of the value‐based adoption model (VAM) and expectancy theory (ET). Across two studies, we uncover the value calculus underlying this behavior. Study 1, a phenomenological analysis of 29 in‐depth interviews with subsistence consumers in eastern India, reveals that adoption decisions hinge on a dynamic trade‐off between two perceived benefits (utilitarian and psychological) and three BOP‐specific perceived sacrifices (opportunity costs, skill constraints, resource limitations). Building on these insights, Study 2 employs the Decision‐Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory method with 10 experts to model causal interrelationships among observed factors. Results identify repair and scarcity as primary drivers, while physical mental strain and time intensity emerge as key barriers. Crucially, jugaad operates paradoxically, as both a coping mechanism and a source of burden, creating a dynamic that facilitates adoption despite its costs. Overall, the findings pioneer value‐based decision‐making in the context of scarcity. Building on these theoretical insights, the study also offers a clear direction for practitioners. Managerially, firms can transform informal resourcefulness into market opportunities by developing repairable, adaptable products that align with BOP consumers' everyday realities and aspirations. For policymakers, the findings illuminate pathways for fostering inclusive circular systems that strengthen consumer capabilities, reduce waste, and enhance community resilience.

latest.title: From Perception to Action: How CSR , Perceived Regulatory Integrity, and Brand Trust Forge Deeper Consumer Bonds in the Hospitality Industry
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: This study investigated the relationships between corporate social responsibility (CSR) perception, perceived regulatory integrity, and brand trustworthiness as well as their combined influence on consumer behavior in the hospitality industry by drawing on the signaling theory. The results demonstrated that positive perceptions of CSR significantly impact perceived regulatory integrity and consumer behaviors, which include customer‐company identification, customer advocacy, and customer citizenship behavior, based on a time‐lagged survey that was conducted with tourists in Pakistan at three intervals, which include sample sizes of n = 345 at T1, n = 260 at T2, and n = 163 at T3. Perceived regulatory integrity was importantly found to mediate the relationship between CSR perception and tourist behavior, such as in particular in relation to identification and citizenship behaviors. Brand trustworthiness also moderated the relationship between perceived regulatory integrity and tourist behaviors, which amplifies the effects of perceived regulatory integrity when trust was high.

latest.title: The psychology of visual branding: how design influences consumer decision-making
latest.venue: RCMOS - Revista Científica Multidisciplinar O Saber
latest.abstract: Visual brand elements — color, logo shape, typography, packaging and the consistency with which they are deployed — shape consumer decisions mainly through three routes: they capture attention, they ease processing, and they carry associations that are transferred to the brand. This review synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence from consumer psychology, marketing and visual neuroscience published between 1968 and 2016. Experimental studies show that hue maps onto brand-personality dimensions (Labrecque; Milne, 2012), that circular versus angular logos shift attribute judgments toward comfort or durability (Jiang et al., 2016), that incomplete typefaces raise perceived innovativeness but lower perceived trustworthiness (Hagtvedt, 2011), and that low-level visual saliency can bias rapid food choices independently of stated preference (Milosavljevic et al., 2012). Across studies, effects are contingent: they depend on congruence with the product category, decision speed, cognitive load and the consumer's existing commitment to the brand. We integrate these findings into a three-stage framework (attention, fluency, meaning) and set out testable propositions. We also flag the limits of the evidence base, including reliance on student samples, short-term outcome measures and widely repeated statistics that lack a traceable empirical source.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer confiden

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Transformasi Ekonomi Digital dan Evolusi Pola Konsumsi: Tinjauan Literatur tentang Perubahan Perilaku Belanja di Era Internet
hot.abstract: Transformasi ekonomi digital telah mengubah pola konsumsi masyarakat secara fundamental, terutama dengan meningkatnya penggunaan e-commerce, layanan berbasis sharing economy, serta metode pembayaran digital yang semakin mempermudah transaksi. Penelitian ini merupakan tinjauan pustaka dengan pendekatan kualitatif dan analisis deskriptif yang bertujuan untuk mengkaji perubahan perilaku belanja di era internet. Data penelitian diambil dari Google Scholar untuk periode 2015–2025, dengan total 50 artikel yang diseleksi menjadi 24 artikel yang relevan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa digitalisasi telah mendorong pergeseran preferensi konsumen dari belanja konvensional ke belanja daring, dengan faktor utama seperti kenyamanan, efisiensi, dan personalisasi layanan. Media sosial dan pemasaran berbasis influencer memainkan peran penting dalam keputusan pembelian, sementara model bisnis baru seperti cloud kitchen dan layanan pesan-antar semakin mengubah pola konsumsi, terutama di industri makanan dan minuman. Namun, fenomena ini juga menghadirkan tantangan, termasuk peningkatan belanja impulsif, risiko keamanan data, dan dampak negatif terhadap sektor ritel tradisional. Implikasi dari penelitian ini menyoroti pentingnya adaptasi bisnis terhadap tren digital, perlunya regulasi yang lebih kuat untuk melindungi konsumen, serta peningkatan literasi digital dan keuangan bagi masyarakat. Penelitian ini memiliki keterbatasan dalam cakupan data sekunder dan tidak menggali aspek demografis atau budaya yang dapat memengaruhi adopsi digitalisasi. Oleh karena itu, studi lanjutan dengan pendekatan empiris diperlukan untuk memperoleh pemahaman yang lebih mendalam mengenai transformasi konsumsi di era digital.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences.
