According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Advancing Sustainable Practices in Electronic Customer Relationship Management
hot.venue: International Review of Management and Marketing
hot.abstract: This paper examines the role of sustainability in determining organisational development and the manner in which it has become a necessity in conducting business. Thus, this research aims at determining the enhancement of sustainable practices in the e-CRM systems. Thus, using surveys and measuring certain e-CRM possibilities quantitatively, interviews and case analyses as qualitative data gathering, the research offers a systemic understanding of how e-CRM may be utilized to encourage sustainability. The preliminary results also reveal a high concern of the respondents towards the sustainability factor in e-CRM with the mean score of 4.2 and considerable awareness of the benefits like cost advantage measure with the calculated score of 4.5 mean. Companies are moderately challenged when it comes to cost and complexity (mean score 3.8) that restrict the integration of sustainability aspect in e-CRM systems, Nevertheless the implementation and planning of sustainability initiative in e-CRM system is high (current initiatives mean score 3.7, planned initiatives mean score 4.1). The qualitative results and cases reveal the ideas, experiences, examples, and quantifiable results, such as a 25% decrease in the usage of paper in the cases and a 30% decrease in energy use. These findings established that e-CRM strategies can be made sustainable, thereby creating improved communication between firms and their customers, whilst mitigating damages to the environment and supporting the long-term sustainability of organisations.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: Authenticity in Influencer Marketing: How Can Influencers and Brands Work Together to Build and Maintain Influencer Authenticity?
hot.abstract: This study examines how different stakeholders perceive influencer authenticity, revealing the misalignments that arise when each group prioritizes different aspects of authenticity. In doing so, the authors generate new theory on influencer marketing and provide managerial insights for brands and agencies to collaborate effectively with influencers to resolve these misalignments and ultimately build and sustain influencer authenticity. Using exploratory, in-depth interviews with consumers, influencers, brand managers, and influencer marketing agencies, the study triangulates stakeholder perspectives on influencer authenticity. Specifically, it examines the misalignment among these groups through the lens of assemblage theory and explores how these misalignments may be resolved to produce successful and lasting influencer assemblages. Finally, it explores how influencer marketing agencies can help manage authenticity misalignments.

hot.title: Cognitive offloading or cognitive overload? How AI alters the mental architecture of coping
hot.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from being a specialized technological tool to an intimate presence in everyday life. Smart assistants organize our schedules, predictive systems anticipate our needs, and therapeutic chatbots promise to listen when no human is available (Zhang & Wang, 2024). The diffusion of AI into mental health care is often framed in highly optimistic terms: technologies that reduce stigma, democratize access, and provide affordable, always-on support (M & N, 2025;Sivasubramanian Balasubramanian, 2023). From meditation applications and emotion-tracking wearables to conversational agents offering cognitive-behavioral interventions, AI is marketed as an efficient and reliable partner in the pursuit of wellbeing (Balcombe, 2023).Beneath this enthusiasm lies a paradox. On one hand, AI enables cognitive offloading: the use of external aids to reduce mental effort and conserve resources for more meaningful activities (Grinschgl & Neubauer, 2022;Risko & Gilbert, 2016). This process can support adaptive coping, helping individuals regulate stress and sustain mental health. On the other hand, the same tools may create cognitive overload: an erosion of introspection, over-reliance on algorithmic feedback, and anxiety induced by hyper-monitoring and optimization (Grinschgl et al., 2021;Skulmowski, 2023). The question is not whether AI is good or bad for mental health but how it is reshaping the very architecture of coping (Gerlich, 2025). This article examines the psychology of this paradox. First, it places copings in mainstream psychological theory. Then it considers the promise of AI to lighten burdens through cognitive offloading. Next, it considers the risks of cognitive overload and theoretical insights that illuminate this conflict. Through practic

latest.title: Toward sustainable agritourism: operational insights from organic farms engaged with tourism
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how integrating organic farming with agritourism can advance sustainable rural development. By examining organic farms engaged with tourism in South Korea through an ecotourism framework, it addresses the need to distinguish genuinely sustainable, ecologically grounded agritourism models from conventional, chemical-intensive practices. Design/methodology/approach The study utilizes a qualitative case study approach combining in-depth interviews with operators of three organic farms and a content analysis of 38 organic farm tourism websites in South Korea. The analysis evaluates farm operations, visitor programming and rural community dynamics against core ecotourism principles, contextualized with recent agritourism literature. Findings Organic agritourism aligns closely with ecotourism by integrating low-impact farming with hands-on environmental education, biodiversity conservation and cultural preservation. Key findings highlight that tourism revenue reinforces organic land stewardship, small-scale operations foster meaningful socio-cultural and educational exchanges and participatory community collaboration enhances rural resilience and local circular economies. Five operational takeaways are identified: ecological conservation, active learning, socio-cultural sustainability, value-based economic viability and inclusive community participation. Originality/value This paper demonstrates that ecotourism serves as an effective guiding paradigm for agritourism on small-scale organic enterprises. It provides actionable operational and policy insights for agritourism operators, planners and government agencies seeking to establish replicable, value-based agritourism models that support environmental integrity, rural vitality and ethical visitor

latest.title: From story to sale: how digital storytelling shapes AR consumers' impulse shopping intention
latest.abstract: Purpose Digital storytelling has emerged as a catalyst and game changer in the transformative marketing ecosystem through integrative efforts with augmented reality. This study addresses this gap by examining how digital storytelling enhances consumer immersion and enjoyment. It also examines the impact of immersion and enjoyment on consumers' impulse shopping intention. Design/methodology/approach 391 responses were collected from active augmented reality users who had experience with brand storytelling in augmented reality. The data were analysed using a combined importance–performance map analysis (cIPMA) in partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The findings demonstrate that the importance of four dimensions of augmented reality digital storytelling (narrative structure, perceived aesthetics, self-reference, theming and storytelling) significantly influences immersion and enjoyment and leads to consumer impulse shopping intention. Furthermore, necessity logic complements sufficiency logic by demonstrating that perceived aesthetics constitutes a necessary condition for both enjoyment and immersion. Theming and storytelling impose a weak bottleneck constraint solely on immersion. Additionally, enjoyment and immersion are less restrictive in practice for impulsive purchase intention. This suggests that most respondents already meet the minimum requirements. Consequently, these antecedents function more as performance-enhancing factors than as critical bottlenecks requiring immediate managerial intervention. Originality/value This study pioneers research at the intersection of augmented reality marketing and digital storytelling by demonstrating how narrative, aesthetics, self-reference, theming and storytelling elements can shape consum

latest.title: Micro-cultural activism in slow fashion: how influencers reframe sustainable consumption on Instagram
latest.venue: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines the activist roles of slow fashion influencers on Instagram, focusing on how they construct and circulate sustainability narratives and reframe sustainable consumption into daily achievable practices. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a qualitative research design, analysing both visual and textual materials from the Instagram posts of slow fashion influencers. Findings The findings reveal that slow fashion influencers operate as micro-cultural activists who perform as educators, advocates and facilitators of ethical consumer practices. By voicing their concerns about workers' rights, animal welfare and textile waste, influencers make complex sustainability issues accessible while encouraging reflection on daily practices such as second-hand shopping, upcycling and recycling. Through their digital narratives, these influencers frame sustainability as an individualized moral identity project, thereby linking their personal consumption choices to lifestyle-oriented ethical advocacy. Research limitations/implications This article contributes to the literature on influencer culture and digital activism by shifting the focus away from short-term behavioural metrics towards cultural meaning-making and demonstrating how influencers use Instagram as a dynamic space for cultural activism. Social implications This paper shows how slow fashion influencers use their digital presence to cultivate environmental, social and ethical awareness among their followers by presenting accessible alternatives to conventional mass consumption. Originality/value This research contributes to the influencer marketing literature by demonstrating how activist roles are enacted through social media and how influencers provide the symbolic tools that enable cons

latest.title: Building productivity in culinary MSMEs through market orientation: the mediating role of value co-creation on marketing performance
latest.venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the impact of responsive and proactive market orientation on the marketing performance of culinary micro, small and medium-sized culinary enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia, positioning marketing performance as a proxy for productivity. Specifically, it explores the mediating role of value co-creation, a mechanism that has received limited empirical attention in prior research. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a quantitative survey approach involving 319 respondents, comprising managers or owners of MSMEs. To evaluate the proposed hypotheses and examine both direct and indirect (mediating) relationships, the data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4. All variables were measured using previously validated measurement scales. Findings Proactive market orientation (PMO) significantly enhances value co-creation but lacks a direct effect on marketing performance; its impact is fully mediated by co-creation. Responsive market orientation (RMO) directly improves performance, and this improvement is partially achieved through co-creation. The study confirms co-creation as a pivotal mechanism linking MO to outcomes, with PMO's influence being entirely indirect and RMO's hybrid (direct/indirect). Originality/value This study advances the literature by integrating responsive and proactive market orientation with value co-creation in the context of culinary MSMEs. It highlights value co-creation as a dynamic capability that enables SMEs to translate market insights into productivity gains despite resource constraints, offering both theoretical enrichment and practical guidance for enhancing competitiveness.

latest.title: DMT-induced aberrant salience and suggestibility correlate with mystical experiences and positive emotionality
latest.abstract: Paradoxically, psychedelics have long been used as models of both psychosis and therapy. After proposing mystical experiences as a link between these models for lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), we aimed to extend and refine this framework for N,N -Dimethyltryptamine (DMT). In a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover study, 25 healthy participants received DMT (60mg) and an active placebo (0.6mg DMT), separated by two hours. Psychotic-like experiences were assessed via aberrant salience (Aberrant Salience Inventory [ASI]) and therapeutic-like experiences via suggestibility (Creative Imagination Scale [CIS]), including suggestion-induced mystical experiences. Psychedelic experiences were measured via the Six Dimensions and Eleven Factors of Altered States of Consciousness Questionnaire (6D-ASC and 11-ASC), Hallucinogen Rating Scale (HRS), and Mystical Experiences Questionnaire (MEQ). Compared to placebo, DMT increased all aberrant salience factors, most suggestibility modalities, including mystical experiences, and most 6D-ASC and HRS factors. Aberrant salience showed widespread correlations with psychedelic experiences, particularly mystical experiences (MEQ) and positive emotionality (e.g., Joyfulness [6D-ASC], Blissful State [11-ASC]). Suggestibility correlated with the same positive emotionality factors and inversely with negatively valenced aberrant salience (Heightened Emotionality [ASI]), emotionality (Dysphoria [HRS), and mystical experiences (Ineffability [MEQ]). In conclusion, DMT’s effects on aberrant salience and suggestibility support its role both as a psychosis and therapy model. The models’ link may be indirect with respect to mystical experiences, with emotionality playing a more crucial role. Importantly, suggestion-induced mystical exp

latest.title: Exploring the relationship between consumer religiosity and perceptions of corporate social responsibility in tobacco companies: Does smoking status matter?
latest.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose Corporate social responsibility (CSR) has become an essential component of corporate strategy, aiming at improving social and environmental outcomes. It is increasingly recognized as a powerful tool for shaping public perceptions of businesses' fair treatment of employees and consumers, addressing social issues, profit orientation, and overall commitment to ethical practices. However, controversial industries are frequently accused of exploiting CSR initiatives. These range from the core “sin” sectors of tobacco, alcohol, and gambling to more contested categories such as fast food and fossil fuels. Such firms often establish their own permissive guidelines under the guise of social responsibility, potentially undermining genuine efforts for positive change. Tobacco, the most consistently classified sin industry, provides the focal context for this study. This study examines how different types of religiosity affect consumers' views on tobacco companies' CSR and their support for these companies, with consumer corporate identity (CCI) serving as a mediator. It also explores how smoking status moderates the relationship between religiosity and CCI. Design/methodology/approach Using a survey of consumers in Indonesia (n = 331), our findings reveal a complex relationship between consumers' religiosity, smoking status, and their perceptions of tobacco companies. Findings Intrinsic religiosity positively shaped CSR perceptions across four of five domains: employee, social, profit, and ethics, with no significant effect on consumer-focused initiatives. Smokers who are more likely to identify with tobacco companies were more inclined to support the CSR initiatives, even disregarding their detrimental effects on society. Extrinsically religious people also show a positiv

latest.title: Reskilling female entrepreneurs for knowledge spillovers: a KSTE perspective on SMEs in lagging regions
latest.abstract: Purpose The research focuses on how territorial innovation aids the process of reskilling and training female entrepreneurs in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through knowledge application and spillover in disadvantaged areas. Based on the knowledge spillover theory of entrepreneurship (KSTE), this study aims to investigate the role of institutional help as an essential tool tying together the development of entrepreneurial competence and application of knowledge. Design/methodology/approach The study uses quantitative research techniques based on structural equation modeling that help identify the correlations between obtaining skills by female entrepreneurs and getting managerial training and implementing innovations in their region concerning knowledge gain and usage. Findings The findings show that territorial innovation enhances entrepreneurial capabilities through reskilling and managerial education, while institutional support facilitates the translation of these capabilities into knowledge application and knowledge spillovers. Firm size and firm age significantly influence knowledge spillovers but do not significantly affect knowledge application. Practical implications The findings of this study will assist policymakers and institutions in developing inclusive reskilling and management education programs for female-owned SMEs based upon knowledge spillovers that lead to true innovations and development in the region. Originality/value The study extends KSTE by embedding it in the context of female-led SMEs in lagging regions, linking entrepreneurial education and territorial innovation to knowledge outcomes.

latest.title: Towards a gender responsive framework to guide social marketers in designing campaigns featuring social media influencers
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how gender norms shape the experiences of social media influencers (SMIs) and consumers when engaging in pro-social initiatives and to develop a conceptual and practical framework to guide social marketers in designing gender responsive campaigns that feature SMIs. This is important because SMIs operating in the pro-social domain face gendered marginalisation that can undermine both campaign effectiveness and SMI safety, yet practical guidance on how to address these dynamics remains limited. Design/methodology/approach The research draws on intersectionality, interpreted using a Caribbean feminist theoretical lens. The authors conducted a multi-method feminist critical discourse analysis of content posted by 40 SMIs, alongside qualitative interviews with 21 SMIs and 20 consumer followers in Trinidad & Tobago. Findings Gender norms rooted in colonial legacies shape how SMIs and consumers experience, interpret and evaluate SMI-led pro-social messages. These dynamics influence perceptions of credibility and effectiveness for both groups. Drawing on participants’ accounts, this study proposes key considerations for a gender-responsive framework focused on SMI follower congruence, stronger representation, leveraging SMIs’ cultural intelligence to enhance engagement with pro-social causes and ensuring consistency in their self-presentation. Originality/value This paper makes a dual contribution. Theoretically, it extends understanding of SMI authenticity and gender-based marginalisation by demonstrating how gendered power, shaped by race, sexuality and class within a Global South context, determines whose voices are seen as credible in pro-social messaging. Practically, it offers the first empirically grounded, gender responsive framework f

latest.title: Queer(y)ing gender in entrepreneurial action through the experiences of transgender women entrepreneurs in Tasmania
latest.venue: International Journal of Entrepreneurial Behaviour & Research
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines and queers entrepreneurial action theory using queer phenomenology, showing how gender affirmation reshapes entrepreneurial action. While entrepreneurial action theory traditionally focuses on decision-making within uncertain environments, it rarely accounts for experiences of transgender women. Design/methodology/approach This research combined narrative inquiry and visual methods to collect data from two transgender women entrepreneurs in Tasmania, Australia. Research on transgender women entrepreneurs is limited, so combined methods capture emotional nuances: (1) drawings of self-perception before and after starting the business and (2) an in-depth interview. Findings Findings suggest considering temporal dynamics across different industries when entrepreneurs seek to reveal their identity. Louise is a mechanical engineer, and being a mechanic in a masculine-dominated industry significantly influences the perceptions of family, friends and customers. Meanwhile, Sally, a comedian, was provided with space for creativity and fluid perceptions. The women's experiences are not uniform, with industries entrepreneurs are aligned with shaping their negotiation of entrepreneurship. Research limitations/implications This study advances entrepreneurial action theory by integrating queer phenomenology to account for transgender women entrepreneurs' lived experiences. It challenges the assumption of time as a neutral construct in entrepreneurial action theory. This study shows how cisnormative expectations within transgender women's space shape entrepreneurial decision-making timing, pacing, and sequencing. Originality/value This article challenges existing discourses around entrepreneurial action theory and gender in entrepreneurship. Transgender wome

latest.title: Reverse logistics in electronics industry: a bibliometric analysis, challenges and future research prospects
latest.venue: Journal of responsible production and consumption.
latest.abstract: Purpose The proliferation of electronic goods has increased challenges for global e-waste; thus, reverse logistics (RL) and closed-loop supply chains (CLSC) in the electronics sector have become very challenging research areas. This study aims to provide a substantial bibliometric and systematic overview of the RL and CLSC research in electronics, with a particular emphasis on identifying potential barriers to implementation and synthesising findings into a conceptual framework for future empirical investigation. Design/methodology/approach Data analysis was performed using the PRISMA 2020 protocol, extracted from the Scopus database through searching the terms reverse logistics, closed-loop supply chain and electronics. The search occurred from 2010 to 2024 and after applying structured inclusion and exclusion criteria resulted in a final corpus of 94 peer-reviewed journal articles. Bibliometric methods, such as trends in publication, keyword co-occurrence, co-citation analysis and thematic mapping, were then used. Findings The volume of publications has grown sharply since 2019, with a combination of the regulators’ attention, the global e-waste crisis and COVID-19 supply chain disruption. Keyword analysis shows a new paradigm shift from operational efficiency to strategic sustainability. There are four dimensions where barriers to RL and CLSC introduction cluster: technical infrastructure gaps, policy and regulatory weaknesses, strategic and organisational resistance and market and consumer behaviour factors. Research limitations/implications Policymakers need to enhance extended producer responsibility (EPR) enforcement and implement market-based incentives. Electronics manufacturers should invest in a phased digital transformation, from RFID-based tracking to AI-en

latest.title: Normalizing sustainable fashion innovations: environmental messages and dynamic norms in circular fashion adoption
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether informational messages promote interest in fashion products made from agri-food waste and whether dynamic norm cues strengthen persuasion in a trend-sensitive, ambiguous market. Design/methodology/approach Overall, 183 Italian adults were randomly assigned to control, environmental message or environmental plus dynamic norm message conditions. Participants reported purchasing intention and willingness to pay a premium price. Pro-environmental self-identity and identification with sustainable fashion consumers were tested as moderators. Findings Only the combined environmental and dynamic norm message increased purchasing intention, whereas neither message affected willingness to pay, suggesting a distinction between motivational interest and financial commitment. Exploratory analyses suggested that the environmental message was more effective among participants with low identification with sustainable fashion consumers. Pro-environmental self-identity did not moderate message effects. Research limitations/implications Self-reported intentions and a highly educated Italian sample limit generalisability. Future studies should use behavioural measures, field experiments, longitudinal designs and diverse samples to test whether initial openness persists and translates into purchasing and price acceptance. Practical implications Environmental messages combined with dynamic norm cues can increase initial interest in agri-food waste fashion, but the promotional strategy did not increase willingness to pay, highlighting the importance of product, price and audience segmentation. Originality/value The study shows that integrating dynamic norm cues into environmental appeals can increase initial openness toward novel sustainable fash

latest.title: Effects of green business practices on business relationships: evidences from the automotive industry
latest.venue: Journal of Business and Industrial Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose The study aims to investigate how the implementation of green business practices (GBPs) – efforts undertaken by firms to reduce their negative impact on the environment, while simultaneously supporting economic and social value creation – influence the substance of business relationships. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, in-depth single case study methodology is applied. Research is carried out within the automotive industrial sector; the unit of analysis is a Portuguese business network which is undergoing a green transition, analyzed through the actors, resources and activities model of the Industrial Marketing and Purchasing approach. Findings The empirical investigation identifies six main effects of GBPs on business relationships: Economic, Innovation, Stability, Leverage, Power and Singularity effects. In addition, elements facilitating the implementation of GBPs are recognized and critically discussed. Originality/value The present research contributes theoretically to widen knowledge on GBPs by examining how their implementation reshapes the substance of business relationships. By exploring how GBPs reconfigure business networks, original managerial implications arise that provide useful directions for practitioners dealing with GBPs.

latest.title: Integrating artificial intelligence into business management: implications for intellectual capital development
latest.abstract: Purpose This study explores the implications of artificial intelligence (AI) integration into business management practices, emphasizing its impact on intellectual capital components. Specifically, it examines how AI integration influences the interaction between human, structural and relational capital in managerial processes. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a rigorous thematic analysis conducted in NVivo. Data collected through an online qualitative questionnaire administered to managers from multiple sectors were analyzed to identify key dimensions of AI integration in business contexts and to develop a conceptual model explaining their interactions. Findings The findings reveal four key dimensions: the role of AI in managerial processes, the challenges associated with AI, the strategies and best practices required to integrate AI into management and the strategies needed to adapt and train human resources in organizations integrating AI. While AI enhances efficiency, automation and decision-making processes, sustainable integration requires strategic planning, gradual implementation and investment in human capital. Overall, AI integration appears to enhance the interaction between human, structural and relational capital rather than radically restructuring intellectual capital. Practical implications The link between technological implementation and human-centered challenges provides practical guidance for organizations undergoing digital transformation. Gradual AI integration through pilot projects, employee training and governance structures supports responsible human–AI collaboration and strategic decision-making. Originality/value This research extends the traditional technology–organization–environment framework by conceptualizing AI integration as

latest.title: Sub-Saharan African agribusiness SMEs' export: What can the resource-based view tell us?
latest.venue: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper investigates the explanatory power of the resource-based view (RBV) of the firm on the agribusiness exports of Sub-Saharan African (SSA) small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Design/methodology/approach Using a qualitative research design, we identify and interpret resources and capabilities by analyzing 16 selected cases describing agribusiness exports by SMEs from SSA. Findings The three most influential resource categories that explain SSA agribusiness exports by SMEs are: (1) Managerial resources, (2) production, technological and R&D resources and (3) marketing-related resources. In most cases, we find resources to drive export decisions and performance in complementary resource “sets”, rather than as singular resources. Research limitations/implications There is potential in moving research beyond the categorization of resources and start working on (contextualized) categorization of resource “sets” that increase the effectiveness of companies' exports. As stipulated by Prahalad and Hamel, the theory of core competencies might be a helpful starting point for investigating complementary resources in the export context. In addition, the complementary resource sets add a dimension of constant change to the RBV discourse. Originality/value We contribute by (1) arguing that the theoretical work of RBV's impact on export needs to move beyond single resources and capabilities towards complementary sets of resources. (2) adding resources not covered prominently in the export literature and (3) investigating a new context (SSA) for the RBV–agribusiness export nexus.

latest.title: Exploring the potential of green waqf as an alternative instrument for climate financing
latest.venue: International Journal of Climate Change Strategies and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the determinants of Indonesian Muslims’ intentions to donate to green waqf, an Islamic financial instrument increasingly used for climate financing. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 550 cash-waqf donors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The model extends the theory of planned behaviour (TPB) by incorporating knowledge, trust, religiosity and environmental awareness into the traditional constructs of attitude, subjective norms and perceived behavioural control (PBC). Reliability, convergent validity and discriminant validity were confirmed. Multicollinearity and predictive relevance were also assessed. Findings The study reveals that knowledge, trust, religiosity and environmental awareness positively influenced attitudes towards green waqf donations. Attitude, subjective norms, PBC and knowledge also directly influence intentions to donate to green waqf, with knowledge emerging as the primary driver. Research limitations/implications The findings suggest that green waqf should be repositioned from traditional philanthropy as a more dedicated climate-financing instrument. This requires strengthening waqf literacy, institutional transparency, impact disclosure and seamless digital channels to translate knowledge, trust and environmental awareness into sustained donation behaviour. These implications are particularly relevant for waqf institutions (nazhirs), waqf authorities and policymakers seeking to mobilise Islamic social finance for climate action. Originality/value This study advances the green waqf literature by extending the TPB to include environmental awareness, knowledge, trust and religiosity. By using a larger and more diverse sample than previous studies, it provides a c

latest.title: The forensic loom: weaving trust and sincerity into the corporation as complex adaptive system
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper introduces the Forensic Loom, a diagnostic framework that treats organizational trust as something that can be verified rather than assumed. It proposes that leadership sincerity, whether a leader is performing the scope they claim, can be examined systematically instead of judged impressionistically. Trust is grounded in what a leader does, not in what a leader is believed capable of doing. Design/methodology/approach The paper is conceptual. It proceeds phenomenologically, grounding a Bohrian complementarity account of the corporation as simultaneously unitary and multiple. It extends Elliott Jaques' stratified systems theory by arguing that five functions are inevitable in any viable corporation. This claim is grounded in Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety. A cybernetic and telemetric architecture, drawn from the tradition of Wiener, Ashby and Beer, operationalizes the framework for measurement. Findings The paper argues that a form of recurring and inevitable failure, which it terms the corporate mask, involves actively performing a scope above one's function and span of discretion. This failure is a rational, locatable source of coordination loss that propagates across hierarchical levels. It is a structural consequence of how formal and functional scopes diverge and never fully close. It proposes level-specific and seam-specific instruments that render this failure measurable and correspond structurally with Beer’s viable system model. Research limitations/implications This paper is conceptual and does not include a case study. The correspondence with Beer's viable system model is structural rather than recursive. A full demonstration that each level recursively embeds the viable system model's own five systems is noted as a direction for future r

latest.title: Factors influencing Elementary-Pre-Service Teacher’s Dispositions Toward Mathematics: An Exploration of Perceptions and Origins
latest.venue: International Journal of Education in Mathematics Science and Technology
latest.abstract: The purpose of this convergent parallel mixed-methods study was to examine dispositions toward mathematics held by elementary pre-service teachers (EPSTs) and to identify factors contributing to their mathematical aversion. Drawing on a productive disposition framework, we analyzed five constructs: self-confidence, perceived value, enjoyment, motivation, and past experiences. Three hundred eighteen EPSTs enrolled in a mathematics methods course participated in the study. Quantitative analyses included descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and chi-square tests. Qualitative data from 177 participants who reported mathematical aversion were analyzed using two-cycle inductive coding procedures. Quantitative results indicated no statistically significant differences in disposition constructs by gender, though a significant difference emerged for perceived value across programs of study. Approximately 56% of EPSTs reported aversion toward mathematics, with origins traced predominantly to elementary and middle school years. Qualitative findings revealed that negative teacher experiences constituted the most frequently cited reason for aversion (25%), followed by low self-confidence (16%) and perceived difficulty (14%). These findings highlight the need for teacher preparation programs to address affective dimensions of mathematical learning and to help EPSTs reconstruct their mathematical identities before entering classrooms.

latest.title: Investigation of the Relationships Among Smartphone Addiction, Recreational Activity Participation, and Leisure Satisfaction with Structural Equation Modeling: A Study on High School Students
latest.venue: International Journal of Education in Mathematics Science and Technology
latest.abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the relationships among high school students' smartphone addiction, recreational activity participation, and leisure satisfaction, to determine whether these variables differ by gender and grade level, and to test the mediating role of recreational activity participation in the relationship between smartphone addiction and leisure satisfaction. The sample of the study, which was conducted with a quantitative research approach in a correlational survey model, consists of 351 high school in Türkiye. Data were collected through the Smartphone Addiction Scale, the Recreation Activity Participation Frequency Scale, and the Leisure Satisfaction Scale. Descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test, one-way analysis of variance, correlation analysis, and structural equation modeling were used in the analysis of the data. The results showed that smartphone addiction negatively predicted leisure satisfaction, whereas recreational activity participation positively and significantly predicted leisure satisfaction. Smartphone addiction was found to be higher in female students and recreational activity participation higher in male students. In line with these results, it is recommended that school-based practices that balance high school students' digital technology use, diversify recreational opportunities, and support quality leisure experiences be developed.

latest.title: Talent management, knowledge management, and transformational leadership: Associations with perceived retention conditions in an Indonesian regional government agency
latest.venue: The Contrarian Finance Accounting and Business Research
latest.abstract: Employee retention is a concern for public agencies whose work requires specialized technical competence, and the Regional Financial and Asset Agency (BKAD) of North Sulawesi Province, Indonesia, has experienced a decline in headcount retention that is concentrated among employees on government work agreements (PPPK). This study examines how perceived talent management, knowledge management, and transformational leadership are associated with perceived retention conditions among current employees. A cross-sectional survey was administered to all 116 eligible staff, comprising civil servants and PPPK employees, and the data were analyzed using multiple linear regression complemented by confidence intervals, robust standard errors, and dominance analysis. The results show that employees who rate each of the three practices more favorably also report more favorable retention conditions, and that the three practices jointly account for a substantial share of the variation in these conditions. However, the practices cannot be ranked with confidence, and the association for talent management is the least robust. Because only employees who stayed were surveyed, the outcome overlaps conceptually with two predictors, and all data come from a single source, the findings describe associations and do not explain why employees left. The study suggests that career development, knowledge sharing, and supervisory leadership should be monitored together, and that future research should complement perception data with exit records and intention-to-stay measures.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Artificial intelligence for customer engagement and brand evangelism: A multi-study approach
MEDIATING EFFECT OF JOB SATISFACTION ON THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN SERVICE INNOVATIONS AND EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE IN DEPOSIT MONEY BANKS IN MUBI, ADAMAWA STATE, NIGERIA
latest.venue: International Journal of African Innovation and Multidisciplinary Research
latest.abstract: This study delves into the intricate relationships between service innovation, job satisfaction, and employee performance within Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) in Mubi, Adamawa state, Nigeria. The banking landscape has undergone profound transformations in recent years, compelling institutions to embrace innovation while simultaneously maintaining employee well-being and performance. The study adopted a survey research design and through meticulous analysis of survey data collected from banking employees using multiple linear regression, this research uncovers interrelated patterns about innovation effects. The result shows that job satisfaction emerges as a partial mediator in the relationship between service innovation and employee performance. This partial mediation suggests dual pathways of influence innovation directly enhances performance through improved tools and processes, while simultaneously boosting satisfaction that further drives performance gains. The mediating role varies across innovation dimensions, adding another layer of complexity to our understanding of workplace dynamics in the banking sector. The DMBs should treat employee satisfaction not as a by-product but as a core strategic lever because this can further be enhanced and institutionalised through regular staff feedback mechanisms, recognition programs, and well-being initiatives.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: The Influence of Advertising Appeal and Brand Image on the Purchase Decision of Makarizo Hair Care Products from the Perspective of Islamic Business
latest.venue: Siber International Journal of Digital Business (SIJDB)
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of advertising appeal and brand image on the purchase decision of Makarizo hair care products in Bandar Lampung City from the perspective of Islamic business. The study uses a quantitative approach with explanatory and associative designs. Data were collected through questionnaires from 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling technique and analyzed using the Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method with SmartPLS 4.0. The results showed that advertising appeal has a positive and statistically significant relationship with purchase decisions (β = 0.327; t = 3.921; p < 0.001). Brand image also showed a positive and significant relationship (β = 0.621; t = 8.805; p < 0.001), with a path coefficient greater than advertising appeal. The coefficient of determination value (R² = 0.796) indicates that both variables are able to explain 79.6% of the variation in purchase decisions in the research model. From the perspective of Islamic business, these findings are interpreted through the principles of honesty (shidq), truthfulness (tabligh), and trustworthiness as normative foundations for ethical marketing. These principles are ethical implications, not empirical evidence of sharia compliance in Makarizo's marketing practices.

latest.title: Customer Engagement towards Loyalty in the context of Influencer Marketing that Leads an Organization’s Resilience in Digital Ecosystems – A Theoretical Perspective
latest.abstract: Influencer marketing has risen from an experimental tactic to a relationship-building mechanism, which is interconnected with digital ecosystems. Influencers are largely used by brands to earn likes, comments and shares, yet this attention span is often very less. This conceptual paper raises the questions as how short-term engagement can convert to customer loyalty, and the contribution of loyalty to enterprise resilience. This study proposes the three-stage framework and ten propositions for integrating the credibility at source level, trust- commitment, customer engagement and dynamic capabilities perspectives. Influencer credibility, authenticity, para social interaction, content relevance and influencer–brand congruence are drivers of engagement; brand trust, commitment and attachment conversion are proposed as mechanisms that convert engagement into brand loyalty, wherein it strengthens the resilience subject to influencer and platform dependency and to ecosystem synergy and turbulence. The observations in this paper links consumer-level relationship outcomes with enterprise-level capabilities, offers propositions for empirical testing drawing managerial implications for sustainable and relationship-centred digital strategies.

latest.title: A Comparative UX Study of Short-Form Video Applications
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The increased number of short-form video contents being created on social media platforms, such as Instagram Reels, has significantly influenced marketing and consumer trends. Many creators now depend on hooks created by them right from the beginning of the video in order to grab the attention of viewers and avoid extremely high drop-off rates. The current research evaluates the impact of vertical vs. horizontal videos on user engagement. Through the assessment of viewer retention and interaction rate among various demographics, it is shown that short-form videos in a vertical orientation provide considerably higher engagement and longer retention times.

latest.title: AS VARIÁVEIS QUE AFETAM O COMPORTAMENTO DO CONSUMIDOR
latest.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
latest.abstract: Consumer behavior can be defined as a set of actions and emotional and mental processes that directly influence the process of choosing, purchasing, and using products and services. In this way, this set of processes will determine how the customer will act when making a purchase. Accordingly, the present work addresses the main variables that affect consumer behavior, from intrinsic to extrinsic factors, and demonstrates, through a case study, why these factors are of great importance to the area of marketing, which promotes significant investment and research by companies. Accordingly, the present study aims to understand the consumer with the aim of offering what they are looking for, whether as a product or an experience.

latest.title: Pengaruh proses seleksi honorer, kontrak kerja, dan turnover terhadap kepuasan kerja honorer Badan Penanggulangan Bencana Daerah (BPBD) Kabupaten Labuhanbatu
latest.abstract: Tujuan – Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dan mengkaji pengaruh proses seleksi honorer, kontrak kerja, dan turnover terhadap kepuasan kerja pegawai honorer di BPBD Kabupaten Labuhanbatu. Desain/metodologi/pendekatan – Penelitian ini bersifat kuantitatif dan melibatkan 42 pegawai honorer sebagai responden. Seluruh tenaga honorer BPBD Kabupaten Labuhanbatu dipilih sebagai subjek penelitian. Data dikumpulkan melalui dokumentasi, observasi, dan survei skala Likert. Analisis meliputi uji asumsi klasik (normalitas, multikolinearitas, dan heteroskedastisitas), regresi linier berganda, uji t, uji F, serta koefisien determinasi. Temuan – Proses seleksi honorer (B = 0,303; p = 0,011) dan kontrak kerja (B = 0,433; p = 0,002) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan secara parsial terhadap kepuasan kerja, sedangkan turnover (B = 0,006; p = 0,970) tidak berpengaruh dan tidak signifikan. Secara simultan, proses seleksi honorer, kontrak kerja, dan turnover berpengaruh terhadap kepuasan kerja tenaga honorer (F = 19,403; p < 0,001). Nilai R Square sebesar 0,605 menunjukkan bahwa ketiga variabel menjelaskan 60,5% variasi kepuasan kerja, sedangkan sisanya dijelaskan oleh faktor lain di luar model. Keterbatasan penelitian – Penelitian hanya dilakukan pada tenaga honorer di BPBD Kabupaten Labuhanbatu dengan 42 responden yang merupakan seluruh subjek penelitian, sehingga generalisasi hasil ke organisasi lain perlu dilakukan dengan hati-hati. Data diperoleh melalui kuesioner skala Likert, dokumentasi, dan observasi, sehingga masih berpotensi dipengaruhi oleh persepsi subjektif. Selain itu, penelitian ini hanya menguji tiga variabel yang memengaruhi kepuasan kerja. latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: INFLUENCE OF BRAND DIFFERENTIATION STRATEGIES ON CUSTOMER PATRONAGE OF AUTOMOBILE PRODUCTS: A STUDY OF TOYOTA AND HONDA MOTOR MANUFACTURING COMPANIES N FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY ABUJA, NIGERIA
latest.abstract: This research analyzed how brand differentiation approaches affect consumer patronage toward automobile brands in Abuja, Nigeria's capital region. The study focused specifically on examining whether the design quality and performance quality of Toyota and Honda cars shape how customers relate to these brands—measured through their confidence in the brands, inclination to buy again, and willingness to recommend them to others. Using a survey methodology, 300 individuals participated in the research through convenience-based selection. Questionnaires were used to gather information, which was then processed using Linear Regression analysis via SPSS 22. The results indicated that both design quality and performance quality of Toyota and Honda automobiles significantly and positively affect customer loyalty toward these brands. The study recommends that company leaders prioritize investment in research and development focused on improving design and performance quality as a key marketing approach to win over new customers and maintain existing ones.

latest.title: A Systematic Review of Cross-Cultural Differences in Consumer Behavior and Effectiveness of Marketing Strategies
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study presents a systematic review of cross-cultural differences in consumer behavior and the effectiveness of marketing strategies, pursuing three objectives: to explore the impact of cross-cultural differences on consumer behavior, to evaluate the effectiveness of marketing strategies in different cultural settings, and to identify best practices for adapting marketing strategies to diverse cultural contexts. The review is based on peer-reviewed articles and industry reports that are published mainly in the last 5 years (from 2022 to 2025). The results revealed that cultural dimensions like those of individualism-collectivism, power distance, and uncertainty avoidance significantly influence purchasing attitudes, brand preference, and advertising appeal, with collectivist markets favoring messages related to community and relationships and individualist markets showing stronger reactions to messages focusing on personal benefit and selfexpression. The findings equally indicated that the effectiveness of advertising, promotion, and digital campaigns was found to be very variable across cultural contexts, with standardized global campaigns underperforming as compared to culturally adapted and hybrid glocalized campaigns in most of the contexts studied. The best practice was found to be a conscious effort to balance generalizability and localization and to involve market-specific research, local partnerships, and culturally intelligent content design. The study concludes that cultural sensitivity is not an afterthought but an integral part of business marketing effectiveness and recommends that businesses develop cultural intelligence skills and engage in glocalized marketing instead of solely standardized or adapted strategies.

latest.title: Pengaruh persepsi harga dan kualitas produk terhadap keputusan pembelian melalui citra merek pada Uniqlo Pekanbaru
latest.abstract: Tujuan – Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh persepsi harga dan kualitas produk terhadap keputusan pembelian, baik langsung maupun melalui citra merek, pada konsumen Uniqlo di Kota Pekanbaru. Fokus ini dipilih karena konsumen fesyen semakin selektif dalam menilai harga, kualitas, dan citra merek sebelum membeli. Desain/metodologi/pendekatan – Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan kerangka stimulus–organisme–respons (S-O-R). Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner daring skala Likert 1–5 dari 105 responden yang dipilih dengan purposive sampling (berdomisili di Pekanbaru, berusia minimal 17 tahun, dan membeli produk Uniqlo minimal sekali dalam satu tahun terakhir). Kecukupan sampel diperiksa dengan analisis power dan metode inverse square root. Analisis memakai SEM-PLS (SmartPLS 4.0), dengan validitas diskriminan diuji melalui kriteria Fornell–Larcker, cross-loading, dan heterotrait–monotrait ratio (HTMT), serta common method bias diuji dengan uji Harman dan VIF kolinearitas penuh. Temuan – Model pengukuran valid dan reliabel (loading factor 0,754–0,893; AVE 0,675–0,785; composite reliability 0,905–0,930). Seluruh HTMT di bawah 0,90, tetapi pasangan citra merek–keputusan pembelian (0,859) melampaui 0,85. Uji common method bias tidak menunjukkan bias yang serius. Persepsi harga (β = 0,424) dan kualitas produk (β = 0,524) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap citra merek. Persepsi harga (β = 0,348), kualitas produk (β = 0,327), dan citra merek (β = 0,394) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Citra merek memediasi secara parsial pengaruh persepsi harga (0,167) dan kualitas produk (0,206) (seluruhnya p < 0,001). Model menjelaskan 69,0% varians keputusan pembelian dan 50,6% varians citra merek. Keterbatasan penelitian – Penelitian terbatas pada

latest.title: What drives social entrepreneurial intention? An integrated model of cognitive, moral, and social antecedents among university students in India
latest.abstract: Social entrepreneurship is pivotal in addressing social and environmental challenges, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying social entrepreneurial intention (SEI), especially in developing nations, remain underexplored. This study, grounded in the Theory of Planned Behaviour and the social entrepreneurial intention framework, investigates the cognitive, moral, normative, and experiential determinants of SEI among higher education students. Employing a quantitative methodology, a cross-sectional design was utilized, involving 349 postgraduate and undergraduate participants. The analysis was conducted using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that opportunity recognition competency (ORC) is the most significant predictor of SEI, underscoring the importance of entrepreneurial cognition in SEI. SEI is positively correlated with social entrepreneurial self-efficacy and subjective norms, indicating the significance of perceived entrepreneurial capability and social endorsement. However, SEI does not exhibit significant associations with empathy, moral obligation, perceived sustainability values, perceived social support, perceived behavioural control, or prior experience. Notably, prior experience is indirectly linked to SEI through social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, despite its direct and total associations with SEI being non-significant. Overall, the findings suggest that opportunity recognition competency, social entrepreneurial self-efficacy, and subjective norms hold greater relative importance for SEI when antecedents are evaluated concurrently.

latest.title: Talk is cheap? Rhetorical nationalism, signal congruity, and government support
latest.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of firms’ rhetorical nationalism in securing R&D subsidies from governments. As signal receivers, government agencies require more than rhetorical signals when assessing firms, given their responsibility for allocating public resources. Drawing on signaling theory, we argue that the effectiveness of rhetorical nationalism depends on signal congruity within a firm’s signal portfolio, that is, the alignment between rhetorical and substantive signals. Using a sample of Chinese high-tech firms, the findings show that rhetorical nationalism is positively associated with R&D subsidies when firms simultaneously engage in philanthropic activities. Conversely, when firms engage in financial misconduct, the effect of rhetorical nationalism weakens, as the misalignment between rhetoric and actions reduces the credibility of the nationalist narrative. This study has implications for signaling theory and organizational nationalism research.

latest.title: Sustainability in Charity Retail: Conflicts in (In)Sufficiency
latest.abstract: Sufficiency has been receiving attention as a means to achieve sustainability. Insights on how to operationalise sufficiency in practice are limited and absent in the context of ecologically constrained organisations, such as, charities. Charities are viewed as critical to sustainability due to their reuse business model; however, charity income is dropping due to the saturation of low-quality and value clothing donations generated by ever-increasing production and consumption of (ultra)fast fashion. This is placing resource (e.g. reliance on volunteer labour) and ecological (e.g. finding reuse routes) burdens on an already constrained sector, highlighting the urgency for charities to future proof the retail businesses foundational to their fundraising efforts. To address this challenge, this research adopts an ethic of sufficiency to introduce business model innovation to charity retail. Drawing on interviews and observations with charity staff, collaborating experts and consumers as donor and retail users, we examine transition to a clothing rental model offering social and ecological sufficiency. We find that the two competing ethics of: (1) sufficiency representing enough and driving deceleration and (2) insufficiency representing not enough and driving acceleration, compete for primacy. While sufficiency can counter challenges arising from insufficiency, competition between them creates contradictory pressures for the charity. This is further exasperated by a misalignment between organisation and consumer experiences of sufficiency. The theoretical and practical implications of the findings for sufficiency, charity retail, rental and consumption are discussed.

latest.title: The Role of Green Marketing of Electric Vehicles in Influencing Buying Intention in Indonesia
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
latest.abstract: This study investigates the role of green marketing in influencing the buying intention of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia. Using a quantitative approach with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), data from 330 respondents across Indonesia were collected via an online questionnaire to assess the relationship between the 4Ps of green marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Electric Vehicle Knowledge, and Environmental Attitude toward Green Buying Intention. The findings reveal that Green Product, Green Price, and Green Place have a significant and positive effect on EV buying intention, while Green Promotion and Electric Vehicle Knowledge did not show a statistically significant impact. Furthermore, although Environmental Attitude was found to have a strong direct influence on Green Buying Intention, it did not significantly moderate any of the tested relationships. The results imply that while Indonesians with strong environmental attitudes are more inclined to purchase EVs, promotional campaigns and general product knowledge from the 4Ps of green marketing may not yet be powerful enough to shift consumer behavior alone.

latest.title: Exploring the Drivers and Barriers for Circular Economy Implementation in the Mining Industry: An ISM Approach
latest.abstract: Mining is an important sector in the development of Indonesian and world civilization. With the largest-ever record of waste volumes and the potential for significant environmental impact, the industry is under constant pressure to maintain and improve environmental performance while remaining economically profitable. This can be achieved by implementing a circular economy. The circular economy is still in its infancy in this sector, and the driving forces and barriers for its implementation are unknown. This study aims to identify the key drivers and barriers and to understand the interactions between factors by using the interpretive structural modeling (ISM) method. This research identified 20 drivers, with the key being the existence of a clear national action plan and technical regulations, and 17 barriers, with the key barrier being the difficulty of incorporating the circular economy as the company's core business. These key factors will assist practitioners and decision-makers in understanding, overcoming, and utilizing them to implement a circular economy in their companies.

latest.title: Consumer Community Formation, Engagement, and Strategic Development in Armenia’s Applied Arts Sector
latest.abstract: This study explores the transformation of traditional Armenian art from passive consumption to active consumer engagement. The paper identifies a structural paradox, known as the “museum trap,” whereby heritage products are highly valued as cultural symbols but remain poorly integrated into consumers’ everyday lives. Using a mixed-method approach, this study employs a research design consisting of a survey of 180 respondents, expert interviews, and a systematic analysis of digital content. The findings were compared with[A1] international standards based on the luxury industry in Europe, the textile industry in Persia, and the Japanese kimono market. The results reveal a gap between the perceived cultural value of heritage products and consumer engagement as reflected in a low Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 13.1% among brand-aware consumers (n = 122). To address this issue, the study proposes a strategic priority matrix that identifies priorities for strengthening branding and transaction transparency. Finally, the findings suggest that fostering an active consumer community requires a dual approach that preserves the cultural significance of traditional crafts while strengthening their integration into contemporary lifestyles.

latest.title: U.S.-Canada Trade Tensions And Their Influence On Canadian Perception, National Sentiment And Consumer Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Business & Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study investigates how recent U.S. threatened and imposed tariffs under the Trump administration have influenced Canadian public sentiment and consumer behaviour. While traditional economic analysis of tariffs focuses on macro-level indicators such as GDP and trade balances, this research explores the sociopsychological and behavioural impacts of economic protectionism on individuals. Specifically, it examines the extent to which Canadian consumers’ awareness of tariffs correlates with negatives perceptions of Americans, increased nationalism, consumer ethnocentrism and retaliatory purchasing behaviour. Drawing upon theories such as social identity theory, consumer ethnocentrism and reactance theory, the study develops a conceptual framework linking tariff awareness to five key hypotheses. A cross-sectional, quantitative survey was conducted with 123 Canadian residents, collecting data on demographic variables, attitudes toward the U.S., national sentiments and purchasing patterns. The validated instruments consisted of both self-developed scales and pre-established scales including the CETSCALE (Shimp & Sharma, 1987) and Kosterman & Feshbach’s Nationalism scale (1989). Statistical analyses revealed significant relationships across several variables. Greater awareness of U.S. tariffs was associated with more negative perceptions of Americans, heightened national pride, a stronger preference for Canadian products and reduced support for U.S. brands. Notably, consumer behaviour in Canada has shifted, with increasing domestic product loyalty and signs of consumer boycott activity, evidenced by retail behaviour. Regression models confirmed that tariff awareness significantly predicts these attitudinal and behavioural outcomes. These findings offer insights into how eco

latest.title: Strategi Pemasaran untuk Meningkatkan Data Saing UMKM Pemindangan Ikan Melalui Inovasi dan Digital Marketing
latest.abstract: Usaha pemindangan ikan di Desa Ngentrong, Kecamatan Campurdarat, Kabupaten Tulungagung, masih mengandalkan pemasaran tradisional berbasis hubungan sosial, sementara persaingan dengan produk olahan ikan modern yang berkemasan dan berpromosi digital semakin ketat. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji strategi pemasaran UMKM pemindangan ikan melalui inovasi produk dan digital marketing, beserta faktor pendukung dan penghambatnya, dalam upaya meningkatkan daya saing usaha. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan wawancara mendalam semi-terstruktur, observasi, dan dokumentasi pada Maret–Mei 2026 terhadap enam informan yang dipilih secara purposive (dua pemilik usaha, dua pekerja, dan dua konsumen). Data dianalisis dengan model interaktif Miles dan Huberman, dilengkapi analisis SWOT dengan matriks IFAS dan EFAS, serta divalidasi melalui triangulasi, member check, peer debriefing, dan audit trail. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa pemasaran masih didominasi penjualan langsung, pengepul, dan word of mouth, tetapi mulai bertransisi ke WhatsApp Business, Facebook, Instagram, dan TikTok. Inovasi produk pada rasa, kemasan, jenis ikan, dan ukuran masih sederhana karena keterbatasan modal, teknologi, dan sumber daya kreatif. Menurut pelaku usaha, digital marketing menambah pelanggan, memperluas pasar, meningkatkan interaksi, dan membangun brand awareness, namun terkendala literasi digital, keterbatasan tenaga, inkonsistensi konten, dan jaringan internet. Skor IFAS 2,90 dan EFAS 2,79 menunjukkan posisi usaha yang cukup baik, dengan strategi SO sebagai yang paling relevan. Daya saing dapat diperkuat dengan mengintegrasikan inovasi produk, digital marketing, dan peningkatan kapasitas pelaku usaha.

latest.title: The Study of Students' Motivation in Learning Law using the Process Approach of First-year students, Faculty of Food Science, Savannakhet University
latest.venue: Scientific Journal of Savannakhet University-ວາລະສານວິທະຍາສາດ ມະຫາວິທະຍາໄລສະຫວັນນະເຂດ
latest.abstract: This research on study of students' motivation learning in Law using a process approach of 1st year in Faculty of Food Science, Savannakhet University, during the 2024-2025 academic year. Including 31 participants, 10 females (representing majors in Agribusiness and Marketing, Food Processing Technology, and Rural Development and Business Promotion) were selected via purposive sampling. The research instruments included lesson plans, pre-tests and post-tests, and a behavioral observation scale covering five dimensions: collaborative planning in group work, mutual assistance among members, enthusiasm and accuracy in data research, group and individual responsibility, and clarity and engagement in presentations. The research followed a one-group pre-test/post-test experimental design. Statistical analysis was conducted using percentages (%), mean (), standard deviation (S.D.), and the Dependent Sample t-test. The findings indicate that the learning outcomes for the Law course using the process approach method were significantly higher in the post-test than the pre-test, with a post-test mean score of () = 7.77 (S.D = 1.54) at a statistical significance level of 0.01. Behavioral observations revealed that students actively participated in activities, demonstrated high responsibility in group tasks, and supported one another. Students showed increased interest and enthusiasm due to the opportunities for self-directed thinking. Regarding attitudes toward the process approach teaching method, the evaluation score was 3.92, categorized at a "Good" level. This method emphasizes teamwork, review and exchange, which aids students in achieving accurate long-term retention. Furthermore, the study on student motivation revealed that both intrinsic and extrinsic motivations were pres

latest.title: The Influence of Work Environment, Coworker Support and Supportive Leadership on Healthcare Workers Performance with Work Engagement as a Mediating Variabel: A Multicenter Study
latest.venue: International Journal of Psycology and Health Science
latest.abstract: This study examines the effects of the physical work environment and facilities, coworker support, and supportive leadership on healthcare workers performance, with work engagement as a mediator. A cross-sectional multicenter survey (27 October to 4 November 2026) of 88 healthcare workers selected by purposive sampling, analyzed with PLS-SEM using SmartPLS. coworker support was positively associated with work engagement (β = 0.308; p = 0.011), whereas the physical work environment (p = 0.334) and supportive leadership (p = 0.197) did not. Work engagement strongly affected performance (β = 0.555; p < 0.001). Only the indirect effect through coworker support was significant (β = 0.171; p = 0.026), and it was borderline in a sensitivity analysis (n = 78; p = 0.052). Coworker support and work engagement play an important role in healthcare workers performance.
