This study develops and tests an integrated framework explaining how Green Franchising (GF), Digital Franchising (DF), and Brand Reputation (BR) influence Sustainable Franchise Performance (SFP), with Relationship Quality (RQ) serving as a relational mechanism and Franchise Typology (FT) capturing heterogeneity across franchise systems. Drawing on agency theory, resource scarcity logic, signaling theory, social exchange theory, the resource-based view, the natural-resource-based view, and contingency theory, the study conceptualizes sustainable franchise performance as a multidimensional outcome encompassing operational, market, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 314 franchise owners and managers directly involved in operating food and beverage (F&B) franchise outlets in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and multi-group analysis (MGA). The results show that GF (β = 0.246, p < 0.001), DF (β = 0.231, p = 0.001), and BR (β = 0.425, p < 0.001) significantly strengthen RQ, while RQ has a substantial positive effect on SFP (β = 0.493, p < 0.001). BR also directly improves SFP (β = 0.187, p = 0.010). In contrast, the direct effects of GF and DF on SFP are not statistically significant, suggesting that green and digital support resources do not automatically translate into sustainable performance but depend substantially on

latest.title: Is AI (Failure) Here to Stay? An Examination of Stability Attributions, Customer Responses, and Repurchase Intentions
latest.venue: DigitalCommons - Kennesaw State University (Kennesaw State University)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly integrated into customer-facing financial services, particularly within the wealth management industry where firms rely on AI-driven systems for portfolio recommendations, fraud detection, customer communication, and financial advising support.While these technologies offer efficiency, they also introduce new forms of service failure that may alter how customers evaluate firms regarding trust, satisfaction, and frustration.Existing service failure and recovery literature has extensively examined customer responses to human-caused failures; however, comparatively less research has explored how consumers cognitively and emotionally process service failures caused by AI systems.More specifically, little attention has been given to whether customers perceive AI failures as temporary incidents or as indicators of broader systemic instability within the firm.This study seeks to examine customer responses to human-and AI-caused service failures in the wealth management industry through the lens of Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), Construal Level Theory (CLT), and Attribution Theory.Specifically, a research model is developed to investigate how perceptions of service failure severity influence attributional stability, defined as the extent to which consumers perceive a failure as ongoing, permanent, and likely to recur over time.The model further examines how stability attributions affect trust, firm satisfaction, frustration, and repurchase intentions following service failures involving either human or AI error.

latest.title: Gender stereotypes and portrayals in advertising: implications for emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals in advertising shape early-stage emotional brand attachment and brand sacredness among young consumers and young adults. It positions gendered advertising as both a branding issue and a responsible-marketing concern in youth-oriented marketplaces. Design/methodology/approach A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 159 valid responses from a Vietnamese sample concentrated mainly in the younger age segment; 83.6% of respondents were aged 14–26. Skincare and automobile advertising stimuli were used to manipulate stereotype congruity and the gender of the focal protagonist. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed relationships. Findings Both gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals significantly influence emotional brand attachment across the experimental conditions. Emotional brand attachment, in turn, positively predicts brand sacredness and its three dimensions: communitas, supremacy and mesmerization. The findings are interpreted as immediate relational and symbolic responses within a youth- and young-adult-oriented sample, not as evidence of fully matured brand attachment or sacredness. Originality/value This study contributes to young-consumer and gender-in-advertising research by extending attention from proximal persuasion outcomes to early relational and symbolic brand outcomes. It clarifies the conceptual distinction between gender role stereotypes and gender portrayals and explains how these cues may shape early-stage attachment and sacredness-related perceptions among young consumers and young adults. The findings also offer responsible-marketing implications: although gendered portrayals may strengthen consumer–brand

latest.title: Marketing verde digital y lealtad hacia las marcas: evidencia de consumidores de Guayaquil
latest.abstract: La sostenibilidad y la digitalización han transformado la forma en que las marcas comunican sus compromisos ambientales y construyen relaciones con los consumidores. En este contexto, esta investigación analiza la relación entre el marketing verde digital y la lealtad hacia las marcas en consumidores de Guayaquil. Se desarrolló un estudio cuantitativo, no experimental y de corte transversal, con una muestra de 106 consumidores mayores de 18 años, seleccionados mediante muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia. La información se recopiló mediante un cuestionario estructurado con escalas Likert de cinco puntos y se analizó mediante modelos de ecuaciones estructurales por mínimos cuadrados parciales (PLS-SEM) utilizando SmartPLS 4. Los resultados muestran una relación positiva y estadísticamente significativa entre el marketing verde digital y la lealtad hacia las marcas (β = 0,687; t = 13,369; p < 0,001). El modelo explicó el 47,2 % de la varianza de la lealtad hacia las marcas (R² = 0,472). Estos resultados sugieren que la comunicación ambiental creíble, la transparencia y las estrategias sostenibles desarrolladas en entornos digitales se relacionan con una mayor lealtad hacia las marcas. El estudio aporta evidencia empírica sobre esta relación en un contexto urbano latinoamericano y plantea implicaciones para la gestión de estrategias digitales orientadas a la sostenibilidad.

latest.title: Opulent and Environmentally Responsible?: Brand‐ and Consumer‐Related Factors Shaping Consumer Responses to Sustainable Product Innovation Signals by Luxury Brands
latest.abstract: Academic Summary Luxury and environmental sustainability often appear fundamentally at odds: luxury derives its value from exclusivity, symbolic aspiration, and resource‐intensive craftsmanship, while sustainability demands restraint, reduced environmental impact, and responsible production. Yet luxury brands such as LVMH and Gucci are increasingly introducing sustainable product innovations, seeking to align with evolving consumer expectations and regulatory demands. For consumers, this creates a genuine tension: does a sustainably produced luxury personal good elevate its desirability, or quietly erode what makes it special in the first place? Despite the urgency of this question for both consumers and brands navigating the luxury‐sustainability interface, research on consumer responses to sustainable product innovation in luxury personal goods remains limited. Drawing on signaling and cue‐diagnosticity theory, this study examines how, why, and when consumers respond to luxury brands'' environmentally sustainable product innovation. Across a pilot and three main experimental studies, it explores consumer responses to sustainability signals, particularly considering skepticism surrounding the sustainability–luxury interface. Results show that consumers have more positive attitudes, higher purchase intentions, and greater willingness to recommend luxury brands engaged in sustainable versus conventional product innovation. This effect is partially mediated by consumers' feelings of specialness, a proximal, state‐like psychological mechanism. Moreover, transparency as a brand‐level signal and socially responsible consumer behavior as a consumer‐level characteristic strengthen the effectiveness of sustainable product innovation signals. These findings advance understanding

latest.title: Emotional Branding: A Comprehensive Literature Review
latest.venue: International Journal Of Applied Management And Economics
latest.abstract: Emotional branding (EB) has evolved from a practitioner-driven marketing (MKTG) philosophy mainly into a substantial stream of academic inquiry that examines how brands cultivate deep, affect-laden bonds with consumers that extend beyond functional attributes and rational appeals. This article offers a comprehensive review of the EB literature, synthesizing conceptual, theoretical, and empirical contributions published between 2005 and 2026. The review first traces the conceptual evolution of the construct, from Gobé's (2001) foundational manifesto to more recent operationalization grounded in brand attachment, brand love (BL), & brand resonance. Then, it examines the theoretical foundations that underpin this specific field, including brand relationship theory (BRT) (Fournier, 1998), attachment theory (AT), self-congruence theory (SCT), and consumer culture theory (CCT), before mapping the antecedents and outcomes of EB identified across qualitative, quantitative, and bibliometric studies. Drawing on evidence from diverse cultural and sectoral contexts, including Jordan, Indonesia, Italy, and the United States, the review demonstrates that EB consistently & positively predicts brand loyalty, brand attachment, customer satisfaction, & purchase share, while also carrying risks such as the emergence of doppelgänger brand imagery when emotional narratives are perceived as inauthentic. This review is concluded by identifying persistent gaps in the literature, particularly regarding cross-cultural generalizability, the measurement of EB as a multidimensional construct, and the paucity of longitudinal and experimental designs, and it proposes a research agenda to address these gaps. latest.title: Effect of Augmented Reality Marketing Strategies on Consumer Brand Performance of Hotels in South-South Nigeria
latest.venue: British Journal of Management and Marketing Studies
latest.abstract: The study examined the effect of augmented reality marketing strategies on consumer brand performance, using a case study of hotels in South-South Nigeria. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from customers of hotels in Edo and Delta States, targeting a population of 312 regular guests. Using Taro Yamane's formula, a sample size of 175 was determined, and purposive sampling was employed to select respondents with AR marketing experience. A structured questionnaire was used as the research instrument. Reliability was confirmed using the test-retest reliability method. Data analysis utilized descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings revealed that interactive product demonstration (ß = 0.330, P < 0.05), virtual product placement (ß = 0.406, P < 0.05), and telepresence (ß = 0.166, P < 0.05) positively affect customer brand performance. The study concludes that augmented reality marketing strategies significantly enhance consumer brand performance in the hospitality industry. These strategies create immersive and engaging experiences that allow customers to interact with hotel offerings in a more personalized and meaningful way. The study recommended that hotels should integrate telepresence features, such as virtual tours and live customer interactions, to create a sense of connection and accessibility, further strengthening customer engagement and satisfaction.

latest.venue: Taiikugaku kenkyu (Japan Journal of Physical Education Health and Sport Sciences)

latest.title: THE IMPACT OF SNACK MODERNISATION ON GENERATION Z CONSUMER ACCEPTANCE
latest.abstract: Snack products have shifted from authentic snacks to modernised ones. This aligns with the culture of Indonesian society, which enjoys eating snacks outside of main mealtimes. Moreover, the target consumers are Generation Z, whose defining characteristics include being visually oriented, easily influenced by social media trends, prone to FOMO, and viewing consumption as part of their identity and lifestyle. This study aims to analyse trends in the modernisation of snacks and their acceptance among Generation Z consumers. The research approach adopted by the researcher is a qualitative approach using field research methods. This method reveals the meanings attributed by members of the community to their behaviour. The key informants in this study were internal informants from the management of the snack industries undergoing modernisation. Additionally, external informants comprised 15 consumers from Generation Z, serving as eligible sources from each selected modernised snack industry. The data analysis technique employed in this study was qualitative data analysis conducted interactively. Once the data had been collected, the processes of data reduction, data display and verification were carried out. The results of the study indicate that the modernisation of snacks has a positive impact on acceptance by Generation Z consumers. This acceptance is due to innovations in terms of taste, product appearance, packaging, ease of consumption and the use of digital media in promotion.

latest.title: From Perception to Action: How CSR , Perceived Regulatory Integrity, and Brand Trust Forge Deeper Consumer Bonds in the Hospitality Industry
latest.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
latest.abstract: This study investigated the relationships between corporate social responsibility (CSR) perception, perceived regulatory integrity, and brand trustworthiness as well as their combined influence on consumer behavior in the hospitality industry by drawing on the signaling theory. The results demonstrated that positive perceptions of CSR significantly impact perceived regulatory integrity and consumer behaviors, which include customer‐company identification, customer advocacy, and customer citizenship behavior, based on a time‐lagged survey that was conducted with tourists in Pakistan at three intervals, which include sample sizes of n = 345 at T1, n = 260 at T2, and n = 163 at T3. Perceived regulatory integrity was importantly found to mediate the relationship between CSR perception and tourist behavior, such as in particular in relation to identification and citizenship behaviors. Brand trustworthiness also moderated the relationship between perceived regulatory integrity and tourist behaviors, which amplifies the effects of perceived regulatory integrity when trust was high.

latest.title: Emotional Attachment Dalam Konsumsi Kopi Reguler Pada Generasi Z di Teluk Kuantan
latest.abstract: Minum kopi secara rutin bagi Generasi Z bisa berarti lebih dari kebiasaan harian yang dibaliknya ada pengalaman rasa nyaman, kebersamaan, dan cara seseorang memaknai dirinya oleh karena itu penelitian ini ingin memahami bagaimana Generasi Z di Teluk Kuantan mengalami dan memaknai kebiasaan ngopi mereka terutama yang berkaitan dengan keterikatan emosional (emotional attachment). Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) dimana data dikumpulkan lewat wawancara semi-terstruktur dengan 10 informan berusia 20-29 tahun. Setiap pengalaman individu ditelaah lebih dulu sebelum peneliti mencari tema yang muncul di seluruh informan dan hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa kopi dimaknai dalam beberapa cara: bagian dari rutinitas, sumber kenyamanan sekaligus waktu rehat, sarana untuk menjalin hubungan sosial, pemicu ketenangan pribadi, dan objek yang menarik karena rasa serta aromanya. Keterikatan emosional pun berbeda-beda di tiap informan, mulai dari kebiasaan yang terasa menenangkan hingga kopi yang menjadi bagian dari pengalaman dan minat pribadi, dengan demikian kopi yang diminum secara rutin memiliki makna emosional yang beragam dan bergantung pada konteks masing-masing. Oleh karena itu temuan ini memperkaya pemahaman tentang keterikatan emosional dalam konsumsi kopi dengan menjadikan pengalaman subjek individu sebagai pusat interpretasi.

latest.title: Unlocking the nexus from innovativeness perceptions to customer loyalty: the roles of omnichannel trust and emotional brand attachment
latest.abstract: Recently, the bonding between consumers and service providers is getting more complex as the current trend shows the importance of innovation for long-run viability. Innovativeness also plays an imperative role in ensuring sustainability for hospitality businesses. Hence, the purpose of this study is to investigate the effects of a holistic concept of innovativeness on trust in omnichannel and behavioral loyalty while the mediating influences of trust in omnichannel of a restaurant and emotional brand attachment on the domain linkages were further explored. This study tested using a structured questionnaire from a sample of chain restaurant customers in Klang Valley area of Malaysia. The results indicate that menu innovativeness, technology-based service innovativeness and experiential innovativeness influence trust in omnichannel. Besides, only dimension of technology-based service innovativeness influences repeat purchase intention while experiential innovativeness influences positive electronic words of mouth (eWOM). Further findings also demonstrated that trust in omnichannel and emotional brand attachment play several important mediating roles in predicting behavioral loyalty. Through application of Stimulus-Organism-Response theory, this study assesses the impacts of innovativeness holistically that employed by restaurateurs, on trust in omnichannel of the restaurant which this perspective has never been explored previously. Apart from making theoretical contributions, this study provides additional insights on practical implications for restaurateurs to invest on salient resources accurately and to innovate their offers more effectively.

latest.title: ЗЕЛЕНИЙ МЕНЕДЖМЕНТ ЯК НАПРЯМ ІННОВАЦІЙНОГО РОЗВИТКУ ГОТЕЛЬНО-РЕСТОРАННОГО БІЗНЕСУ
latest.abstract: Досліджено теоретичні та прикладні засади впровадження зеленого менеджменту на підприємствах сфери HoReCa в Україні. Обґрунтовано доцільність обрання сфери HoReCa об’єктом дослідження через комплексне використання ресурсів та пряму взаємодію зі споживачами. Систематизовано принципи зеленого менеджменту: ресурсоефективність, превентивність, екологічну відповідальність, інноваційність та системність. На основі емпіричного дослідження (анкетування 18 підприємств HoReCa) виявлено основні бар’єри зеленої трансформації: фінансові (72%), кадрово-поведінкові (56%), інформаційні (44%), організаційні (39%). Запропоновано авторську класифікацію бар’єрів за масштабом підприємства. Розроблено інтегральний індекс зеленої трансформації підприємства (10 показників) та диференційовані заходи зеленого менеджменту для малих, середніх і великих підприємств. Доведено необхідність сприйняття зеленого менеджменту як комплексної управлінсько-інноваційної системи. Практичне значення полягає у можливості використання запропонованих заходів для планування екологічних заходів підприємствами HoReCa. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає у розробленні інтегрального індексу зеленої трансформації, удосконаленні класифікації бар’єрів на основі емпіричних даних та обґрунтуванні диференційованого механізму впровадження зеленого менеджменту залежно від масштабу підприємства.

latest.title: Beyond resistance: deinfluencing, consumer activism and the incorporation of critique on digital platforms
latest.abstract: Deinfluencing is a social media trend where content creators advise audiences not to buy ‘must-have,’ overhyped, overpriced, low-quality, or unnecessary products. It serves as a potential form of resistance to the logic of overconsumption. Gaining momentum on TikTok in early 2023, deinfluencing rapidly spread across social media platforms where the meanings and norms of consumption are publicly negotiated and can acquire collective relevance. This conceptual paper proposes a critical reading of the phenomenon, arguing that deinfluencing does not necessarily constitute a negation of influencer marketing, but may instead be incorporated into the commercial arrangements it contests while retaining critical meanings and effects. Situated at the intersection of consumer culture, consumer activism, influencer marketing and platformisation, the paper examines the infrastructural and commercial conditions through which consumer critique acquires visibility and value. It develops a multilevel conceptual model comprising three analytically distinct but potentially overlapping mechanisms through which critical discourse can be incorporated into influencer marketing: substitution , at the content level, whereby criticism of particular products redirects rather than rejects consumption; hybridisation , at the level of practices, whereby influencing and deinfluencing coexist within creators’ communicative repertoire; and authenticity renewal , at the level of audience relations, whereby rejecting some products can strengthen creator credibility and, under certain conditions, the persuasive value of subsequent endorsements. Platformisation conditions the circulation and visibility of these critical practices without determining their effects. Drawing on the sociological concept of bou

latest.title: The Role of Emotional Attachment in Mediating the Influence of Parasocial Interaction on Impulsive Buying (Study on BTS Fans in Denpasar City)
latest.abstract: The growing popularity of the Korean Wave (Hallyu) in recent years has contributed to increased consumption of South Korean popular culture products, particularly Korean pop (K-pop), across various countries, including Indonesia. The global popularity of BTS has fostered strong emotional connections between fans and their idols through digital interactions on social media platforms. These interactions may facilitate the development of parasocial relationships and emotional attachment, potentially influencing fans' consumption behavior, including impulsive buying. This study aimed to examine and explain the mediating role of emotional attachment in the relationship between parasocial interaction and impulsive buying among BTS fans, collectively known as ARMY, in Denpasar City, Indonesia. The study population comprised BTS fans residing in Denpasar City, from whom 120 respondents were selected using a nonprobability purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.0. The findings revealed that parasocial interaction had a positive and statistically significant effect on impulsive buying and emotional attachment. Furthermore, emotional attachment had a positive and statistically significant effect on impulsive buying and partially mediated the relationship between parasocial interaction and impulsive buying. These findings highlighted the importance of parasocial interaction and emotional attachment in explaining impulsive buying tendencies among BTS fans. The study provided insights into the psychological mechanisms underlying fan consumption behavior and offered practical implications for marketers seeking to understand consumer engagement and purchasing decisions within digital fa

latest.title: Ảnh hưởng của truyền thông mạng xã hội đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch của thế hệ Gen Z tại Việt Nam
latest.abstract: Nghiên cứu phân tích ảnh hưởng của truyền thông mạng xã hội đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch của thế hệ Gen Z tại Việt Nam. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp định lượng, dữ liệu được thu thập bằng khảo sát trực tuyến thông qua Google Forms đối với những người thuộc thế hệ Gen Z có sử dụng mạng xã hội để tìm kiếm, xem hoặc tương tác với nội dung về điểm đến du lịch. Sau quá trình sàng lọc và làm sạch dữ liệu, 214 phiếu hợp lệ được sử dụng để phân tích bằng phần mềm SPSS 27.0 thông qua các kỹ thuật kiểm định độ tin cậy Cronbach's alpha, phân tích nhân tố khám phá và hồi quy tuyến tính bội. Kết quả cho thấy chất lượng thông tin, nội dung do người dùng tạo ra và mức độ tương tác đều ảnh hưởng tích cực đến nhận thức thương hiệu điểm đến du lịch; trong đó nội dung do người dùng tạo ra có tác động mạnh nhất. Nghiên cứu bổ sung bằng chứng thực nghiệm về vai trò của truyền thông mạng xã hội trong xây dựng thương hiệu điểm đến và đề xuất hàm ý định vị điểm đến Việt Nam theo hướng trực quan, tương tác, đáng tin cậy và phù hợp với Gen Z.

latest.title: The relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust: brand credibility, emotional attachment, and perceived quality effects
latest.abstract: Introduction The purpose of this research was to explore the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Specifically, we developed a conceptual model which proposes that brand credibility has a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust, and that perceived quality and emotional attachment have mediating effects on brand trust. Methods We tested the conceptual model by conducting a 2 × 2 (low versus high brand ethicality and low versus high brand credibility) between-subjects experiment, with brand trust as the dependent variable. Data ( N = 208) were collected at a large university in Bangladesh, and were analysed using PLS-SEM. Results Results of the experiment suggest that brand ethicality has a direct effect on brand trust. Brand ethicality also enhances emotional attachment and perceived quality, which, in turn, lead to increased brand trust. Brand credibility, however, does not have a moderating effect on the relationship between brand ethicality and brand trust. Discussion Drawing on signalling theory, the findings provide causal evidence that brand ethicality builds brand trust through two parallel pathways: an affective pathway via emotional attachment and a cognitive pathway via perceived quality. Contrary to expectations, brand credibility did not act as a boundary condition, suggesting that brand ethicality and brand credibility may be better understood as sequential antecedents of brand trust rather than as interacting constructs. For practice, marketers ought to increase brand ethicality to increase brand trust, both directly and via emotional attachment and perceived quality.

latest.title: How is AI companionship reshaping young consumers’ emotional engagement and future brand relationships in digital marketing?
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital marketing by shifting engagement from transactional interactions to emotionally driven relationships. This practitioner viewpoint aims to explore the rise in AI companionship, including conversational agents, virtual influencers and emotional responsive AI systems, and their role in shaping young consumers’ engagement within digital ecosystems. These technologies enable human-like emotional interaction, fostering trust, attachment and sustained relational bonds between young consumers and AI-mediated brand environments. Design/methodology/approach This article draws on a purposive selected body of recent and seminal literature on consumer psychology to explain how parasocial interactions, anthropomorphism and emotional attachment increasingly influence young consumer-brand relationships. The literature was selected based on its relevance to the study objectives, conceptual contribution and practical implications for marketing. The reviewed studies were synthesised into connected themes, which originally provided the foundation for developing foundational practical and managerial implications presented. Findings It highlights strategic opportunities such as hyper-personalisation, continued engagement and customer value creation, while also identifying governance challenges related to transparency, emotional manipulation, data ethics and consumer vulnerability. Practical implications The viewpoint synthesises these developments into young consumers psychological transformation, strategic implications and socio-technical governance challenges. It further outlines future scenarios where AI companions become embedded actors in digital marketing ecosystems, fundamentally transforming both professional practice and soci

latest.title: Role of corporate social responsibility in brand loyalty, emotional attachment and online behavior among Generation Z consumers: a cross-national study
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the triple bottom line (TBL) framework and social identity theory (SIT), this study aims to examine how Generation Z consumers’ perceptions of the economic, environmental and social dimensions of corporate social responsibility (CSR) relate to brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, and how these relationships extend to electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) and online brand-related activities across national contexts. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 815 Generation Z consumers in Chile, Germany, Austria and Greece. Structural equation modeling was used to examine relationships among the three CSR dimensions and brand loyalty, emotional brand attachment, eWOM and online brand-related activities. Multi-group analysis was conducted to assess cross-national differences. Findings Environmental and economic CSR are positively associated with brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, whereas social CSR is negatively associated with brand loyalty and has no significant effect on emotional brand attachment. Brand loyalty positively influences eWOM, while emotional brand attachment positively influences online brand-related activities. Most structural relationships vary significantly across countries, although the relationship between emotional brand attachment and online brand-related activities remains consistent across countries. Originality/value The study advances CSR research by treating CSR as a multidimensional set of signals rather than a homogeneous construct and examining their differentiated implications for consumer–brand relationships. Integrating TBL with an identity-based perspective from SIT, it shows that different CSR dimensions may carry different relevance for Gen Z consumers, and that their effects vary across natio

latest.title: Designing transparency in AI influencer marketing: a consumer–agency architecture
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to develop an understanding of AI influencer transparency and its effects on affective and cognitive trust, engagement and consumer well-being. Design/methodology/approach This paper presents a conceptual synthesis of influencer marketing, consumer psychology and human–algorithm interaction research. Findings This paper introduces the Consumer–Agency Architecture (CAA) framework, distinguishing between information, control and provenance transparency. CAA posits that effects of transparency on consumer outcomes are driven by reductions in reactance, whether affective or cognitive. Information transparency primarily mitigates affective reactance; control transparency reduces cognitive reactance; and provenance transparency can attenuate both. Lower reactance, in turn, can support the formation of affective and cognitive trust, engagement and consumer well-being. The framework further identifies boundary conditions that either strengthen or weaken the relationship between transparency and reactance. Research limitations/implications This paper proposes a conceptual framework that remains to be empirically tested. It also posits that transparency effects in AI influencer marketing are primarily driven by reactance, not gains in perceived authenticity. The developed model also assumes that transparency forms have distinct rather than additive or even nonlinear effects on cognitive and affective reactance. Such assumptions could be tested in future work. Practical implications Brands and platforms should treat transparency as a portfolio of design levers rather than a single disclosure: match the specific type of transparency to the focal objective, anticipate trade-offs and avoid one-size-fits-all transparency that can erode trust. Socia

latest.title: Digital nostalgia and purchase intention among young consumers: roles of attachment, authenticity and brand trust
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to understand how nostalgia proneness and social media engagement influence consumers’ emotional attachment, perceived authenticity, brand trust and purchase intention in digitally mediated, hyper-connected environments. Based on the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) framework, nostalgia proneness and social media engagement are treated as stimulus factors; emotional attachment and perceived authenticity as organism factors; and brand trust and purchase intention as response factors. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted using survey data collected from 501 consumers across multiple sectors in India. Structural equation modeling was used to test the proposed conceptual framework and examine the direct and mediating relationships among the constructs. Findings Results show that nostalgia proneness positively impacts consumers’ emotional attachment and perceived authenticity. Social media engagement positively affects emotional attachment. Emotional attachment and perceived authenticity significantly predict brand trust, which leads to higher purchase intention among consumers. In addition, emotional attachment fully mediates the impact of nostalgia proneness on consumers’ brand trust. The study contributes to emerging digital nostalgia literature by explaining how algorithmically mediated nostalgic experiences influence young consumers’ emotional and behavioral responses, Gen Z and Millennials in particular. Research limitations/implications First, the study used a cross-sectional research design. A causal relationship among the study’s variables cannot be concluded because of its cross-sectional nature. Researchers can use longitudinal studies in the future to understand nostalgic exper

latest.title: Digital entrepreneurship challenge: the effect of website/app hopping on information usefulness
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine website/app hopping as a digital entrepreneurship challenge that shapes consumers' perceptions of information usefulness. Specifically, the study investigates how Generation Z (Gen Z) consumers' digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products relate to website/app hopping and how website/app hopping is associated with information usefulness. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a two-study mixed-method design. Study 1 draws on semi-structured interviews with 12 small business entrepreneurs to identify key themes related to Gen Z consumers' website/app hopping. Study 2 tests the resulting model using survey data from 314 US Gen Z consumers aged 18–24, analyzed through exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling and multi-group moderation analysis. Findings The results show that pragmatism and preference for curated products positively predict website/app hopping, while digital savviness might serve as an enabling condition rather than a direct motivator. Website/app hopping is positively related to information usefulness. Multi-group analysis shows that for low-frequency shoppers, digital savviness, pragmatism and preference for curated products all predict website/app hopping. For high-frequency shoppers, pragmatism is the only significant predictor. These findings suggest that digital savviness may be an enabling condition, while pragmatism is the primary motivational driver. Originality/value This study contributes to digital entrepreneurship by reframing website/app hopping as an entrepreneurial information-management challenge rather than merely a consumer search behavior. It shows how Gen Z consumers verify information across fragmented digital platf

latest.title: Between emotion and ethics: a review of advertising appeals, communication and socially responsible consumption (SRC)
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to provide a literature review of the role of advertising appeal and communication on socially responsible consumption (SRC). It synthesizes 75 peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus and/or SSCI from the period of 1990–2025. Design/methodology/approach This review adopted a multi-source, iterative search process, incorporating searches via databases, keyword/journal searching, Google Scholar and backward citation searches. Conducted on August 15, 2025, the search provided partial coverage of 2025 publications. Three-stage screening and author-led quality appraisal were applied. The selected articles were analyzed by publication year, geographical context, methodology, respondent characteristics, theoretical framework and advertising appeal themes. Findings The review reveals a transition from traditional rational-emotional appeals toward integrated sustainable, digital, influencer and identity-based communication. Green and corporate social responsibility appeals emerged after 2010, whereas digital and influencer-based persuasion has been gaining prominence since 2015. Emotional and social appeals tend to produce more persuasive results compared with rational appeals, depending on such factors as credibility, authenticity, culture, generations, consumer identity and communication context. Practical implications The results will assist marketing experts, policymakers and communication strategists in creating context-based, credible, authentic and emotional campaigns aimed at promoting socially responsible behavior. Originality/value This review provides an analysis of fragmented literature on advertising appeals by applying the SRC approach, which highlights the idea that no single appeal is universally effective. Instead, the outcomes depend on

latest.title: How the Use of AI-Generated Advertising Affects Generation Z Consumers' Brand Trust and Purchase Intentions
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: While generative artificial intelligence (AI) offers a great means to produce advertising copy, images, and videos rapidly, continuously, and at scale, its effectiveness is contingent on consumers' perceptions of the human and the human processes that influence the creation of the ads. It aims to grasp the extent to which the AI-generated advertisements can impact the purchase intent and brand trust of Generation Z consumers. It discusses the difference between results from AI-generated ad copy and identifying the fact that the copy was created with artificial intelligence, as well as combining data from advertisement experiments, canvassing, social media research, and a Generation Z survey (with varying samples and outcomes). Research in the literature indicates that the 'fitness', authenticity, credibility, and interpretation of disclosure are more effective in determining responses than sole AI authorship. One of the most likely courses to achieve the intention to buy, and one that few studies address with an eye on Generation Z, is trust. The recommendations of the review are a holistic approach, the consideration of threshold effects of causality, as well as transparent and correct advertising, not only with regard to advertising but also to show clear responsibility of the human being.

latest.title: Co-designing with Generative AI: consumer participation behaviour and product authenticity
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping consumer–brand interactions, with fashion brands increasingly adopting Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) co-design tools that enable direct consumer participation in product design. This research examines how consumers evaluate the authenticity of the GenAI co-designed products, and how evaluation influences consumers’ future participation with fashion brands. This study further investigates whether consumer self-efficacy and perceived expertise toward the tools serve as key antecedents of the authenticity perceptions. By focusing on an emerging AI-enabled service (GenAI) context, this study expands consumer participation and value co-creation research by offering new insight into the drivers and consequences of the perceived authenticity of the fashion products co-created by GenAI and consumers.

latest.title: A consumer neuroscience approach to examining how augmented reality and QR codes support product and brand sustainability communication in retail settings
latest.abstract: This research explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Quick Response (QR) codes as tools for communicating sustainability-related information in a quasi-realistic retail setting. It combines neurophysiological and self-report measures to investigate how these technologies influence consumers’ sustainability perceptions, emotional engagement, and cognitive workload. Participants took part in a simulated shopping experience, where they were exposed to one of three experimental conditions: traditional packaging, smartphone-mediated QR code scanning, and smartphone-mediated Augmented Reality exploration of coffee packaging. Cognitive workload (measured via electroencephalography) and emotional engagement (measured via skin conductance and heart rate) were recorded alongside self-report measures of green company orientation (GCO), green product informativeness (GPI), and brand familiarity. Findings indicate that while both AR and QR codes evoke more positive emotions and lead to higher perceptions of GCO and GPI, AR usage is also associated with higher cognitive workload. Additionally, brand familiarity enhanced self-report scores but not neurophysiological ones, without interacting with the interaction modality. This research provides a multi-level (implicit neurophysiological and explicit self-reported) perspective on the impact of digital packaging formats on sustainability communication. The findings contribute to ongoing discussions on how interactive technologies can support effective communication, implicit emotions, and consumer engagement with sustainability in retail environments.

latest.title: Canine Companions in the Digital Age: Exploring Pet-Centric Social Media through the Lens of the Extended Self Theory
latest.abstract: This study investigates how Dutch dog owners use non-commercial Instagram profiles for their dogs and how managing these profiles relates to identity construction and self-perception. Guided by Belk’s Extended Self Theory, the study employed a cross-sectional qualitative design and semi-structured interviews with 10 Dutch women who actively managed Instagram accounts for their dogs without seeking monetization. Narrative analysis focused on structure, style, identity, context, and theme, followed by thematic analysis. Five themes emerged: memory preservation; the human-pet bond; social interaction and community; expression and identity; and consumer behavior and pet products. Participants described Instagram as a digital archive for shared memories, a medium for presenting dogs as family members, a site for developing relationships and support networks, and a space for expressing personality, values, humor, and expertise. The accounts also exposed participants to pet products and peer recommendations, influencing consumer knowledge and behavior. Taken together, the findings indicate that pet Instagram profiles operate as digital extensions of owners’ selves, linking personal identity with the represented identity of the dog and with the social networks surrounding the account. The study extends discussion of the Extended Self Theory into everyday, non-commercial pet-centered social media use.

latest.title: The Impact of Scarcity Strategies on Consumer Purchasing Behaviour: A Case Study of Dubai Chocolate
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: In the digital economy, scarcity marketing and social media amplification shape consumer buying behaviour, and viral food products offer a compelling empirical context. This research will investigate the emergence of Dubai Chocolate and the role of scarcity and social media in consumer purchase behaviour. The research examines how FIX Dessert Chocolatier's limited supply helped establish its perceived exclusivity, value, and curiosity, and how TikTok and influencer marketing quickly increased awareness and demand. These strategies also brought risks, including paying too much for scarce items, buying out of FOMO, confusion, and herd mentality with imitating items. The study suggests solutions for these problems: increase price transparency and official restocking systems, increase authenticity in social media marketing, and increase product authentication and supply-chain transparency. The results indicate that creating scarcity can help build consumer interest and can help spur rapid growth for a brand, yet too much scarcity and FOMO can lead to decreased consumer trust and spur less calculated purchases. Hence, businesses should weigh the pros and cons of exclusivity while maintaining clear communication and consumer safeguards. The study offers actionable takeaways for viral brands looking to deploy social media and scarcity tactics to sustain their consumer relationships.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer confiden

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation. This study aims to examine the impact of digital transformation on the marketing performance of small and medium enterprises. This research seeks to fill this void by adopting the technology adoption model in order to explore how in a fast-changing technological environment, digital transformation plays its role in firm specific capabilities that are imperative for a firm to adopt, and how they impact firm’s marketing performance. Combination of convenience sampling as well as snowball sampling was used to collect the data. Utilizing survey data from 316 small to medium-sized enterprises in the twin cities (Islamabad & Rawalpindi), Pakistan the results indicate that digital transformation has a positive influence on small and medium enterprises’ marketing performance. This encourages businesses to take advantage of the opportunity presented by new digital technologies and industry-wide digitalization trends by adopting new technologies and improving their digital capabilities in order to increase their productivity, efficiency, and innovation as well as their marketing performance. Hence this study is a practical demonstration of how developing digital transformation may be used to develop novel digital products and services and thereby improve marketing performance that leads to the overall corporate performance. Finally, the study contributes to the literature by evaluating the proposed model that describes the relationships between digital transformation, social media marketing, market turbulence and marketing performance concurrently.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: The Impact of Green Perceived Value Through Green New Products on Purchase Intention: Brand Attitudes, Brand Trust, and Digital Customer Engagement
hot.abstract: This study examines how the introduction of green new products (GNPs) by luxury brands contributes to building brand equity (i.e., brand attitude and trust) through green perceived value (GPV) and empirically assesses its impact on consumers’ purchase intentions. Furthermore, it explores the moderating role of digital customer engagement (DCE) in the relationship between GPV and building brand equity. To verify the hypothesis, we performed the partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) as an analytical technique using 572 datasets from luxury consumers in China. The results revealed that GPV through GNPs significantly influences both brand attitude and brand trust. In addition, brand attitude and brand trust were found to have a significantly positive effect on purchase intention. Moreover, DCE was observed to positively moderate the relationship between GPV and brand trust. To enhance the purchase intentions for luxury brands, it is essential to foster brand attitude and brand trust by developing a multidimensional GPV through GNPs. Furthermore, DCE plays a crucial role in strengthening the brand trust component of GPV.

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: Impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior: role of credibility, perceived authenticity, and sustainability
hot.abstract: Introduction Social media advertising is a crucial factor for predicting consumer behavior. Further credibility, authenticity, and sustainability of social postings enhance consumer purchase intentions in general and online shopping in particular. This empirical study investigated the impact of social media advertising on consumer behavior and the role of credibility, perceived authenticity and sustainability. The study also investigated the mediating effect of trust in the relationship between social media advertising and consumer behavior. Methods To measure the impact of the social media advertising effect on consumer behavior, eight reflective constructs, namely, credibility, sustainability, perceived authenticity, social media advertising effectiveness, satisfaction, purchase intentions and perceived value, were assessed. For the mediation analysis, consumer behavior was modeled as a higher-order construct with three sub-dimensions: satisfaction, perceived value and purchase intentions. Furthermore, the construct social media effectiveness is also modeled as a higher-order construct with four sub-dimensions: credibility, sustainability, authenticity and social media advertisement effectiveness. The data were collected from active social media users who engage in brand advertising and online shopping. A total of 500 valid responses were subjected to exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and the hypotheses were tested via structural equation modeling. Results and discussion The SEM results reveal that constructs credibility and sustainability are strong predictors of consumer behavior in the context of social media advertising effectiveness. The mediating variable of trust partially mediated the relationship between social media effectiveness and consumer beh

hot.title: Effective Advertising and its Influence on Consumer Buying Behavior
hot.abstract: Advertising is a way of communication to convince an audience for taking purchase decision about a product or service and delivering information to viewers. This paper examines the relationship between environmental response and emotional response which are independent variables with dependent variable i.e. consumer buying behavior. This research investigates the relationship between the variables involved, by taking the 200 responses in twins’ cities of Pakistan. Findings of this study show the moderate relationship between independent variables and dependent variable. It shows that consumer purchase those brands from which they are emotionally attached. This study reports new results in the field of buying behavior of consumers’ response.

hot.title: Authenticity in Influencer Marketing: How Can Influencers and Brands Work Together to Build and Maintain Influencer Authenticity?
hot.abstract: This study examines how different stakeholders perceive influencer authenticity, revealing the misalignments that arise when each group prioritizes different aspects of authenticity. In doing so, the authors generate new theory on influencer marketing and provide managerial insights for brands and agencies to collaborate effectively with influencers to resolve these misalignments and ultimately build and sustain influencer authenticity. Using exploratory, in-depth interviews with consumers, influencers, brand managers, and influencer marketing agencies, the study triangulates stakeholder perspectives on influencer authenticity. Specifically, it examines the misalignment among these groups through the lens of assemblage theory and explores how these misalignments may be resolved to produce successful and lasting influencer assemblages. Finally, it explores how influencer marketing agencies can help manage authenticity misalignments.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing Within the Framework of Sustainable Management
hot.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not only revolutionizing digital marketing through personalized customer experiences and optimized advertising strategies, but it is also contributing to sustainability initiatives. As AI reshapes digital marketing, its impact on sustainability is becoming increasingly significant. This dynamic highlights the necessity of exploring how AI can be utilized to foster more sustainable marketing practices. This study seeks to answer the pivotal question: “How does AI impact the sustainability of digital marketing?” A systematic literature review was conducted in this study, following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework to identify various relevant articles in the areas of sustainability and marketing. Furthermore, this study examines the crucial role of AI in enhancing sustainable business practices, highlighting a significant increase in adoption among enterprises. The findings demonstrate that the effective integration of AI into digital marketing enhances environmental sustainability, supports the attainment of economic sustainability objectives, and contributes positively to social sustainability outcomes. This study contributes to the field by providing a comprehensive analysis of the intersection between AI and sustainable marketing practices and offers valuable insights for marketers, businesses, and policymakers.

hot.title: The Evolution of Digital Tourism Marketing: From Hashtags to AI-Immersive Journeys in the Metaverse Era
hot.abstract: This study examines how social media platforms influence tourism marketing strategies, consumer perceptions, and travel behaviors, addressing their sustainability implications. It aims to evaluate the current state of research on social media in tourism marketing, identify dominant trends, assess empirical evidence of impact, and critically highlight research gaps. The analysis focuses on three core marketing outcomes: destination image, travel intention, and user engagement—and includes a section examining sustainability considerations across environmental, sociocultural, and economic dimensions. The study uses a systematic critical review of 147 peer-reviewed academic articles published between 2015 and 2025, combined with a meta-analysis of 38 quantitative studies that report statistical effect sizes. The meta-analysis uses a random-effects model to compare the influence of different platforms and study contexts. Moderator variables include geographic region, platform type, and methodological design. Findings show that social media marketing has a statistically significant positive effect on destination image (Cohen’s d = 0.61), travel intention (d = 0.54), and user engagement (d = 0.43). The analysis also reveals geographic bias, limited research on emerging platforms, and a lack of longitudinal and ethical inquiry. Findings suggest that tourism researchers and marketers may have to adopt more context-sensitive, interdisciplinary, and ethical approaches. Critical sustainability concerns emerge, including “overtourism”, cultural commodification, digital inequities, and algorithmic biases. Further studies may focus on specific platform-related behaviors, long-term impacts, and integrated online strategies appropriate for global tourism diversity. Lastly, this paper ad

hot.title: Digital Tourism and Smart Development: State-of-the-Art Review
hot.abstract: The intersection between digital technologies and tourism emerges as a prominent area of research within the tourism industry. This is primarily driven by the immense complexity of digital tourism itself as a multifaceted social, economic, and cultural phenomenon. This paper reveals the future implications of tourism in the context of digital intelligence. To gain insights into the latest applications of digital tourism, this work reviews 278 studies spanning from 2012 to 2024. A systematic literature analysis method is proposed to identify the research hotspots and trends. Through value co-creation theory and Schumpeter’s innovation theory, five key trajectories are suggested, as follows: in-depth application of digital technologies in tourism, spawning new scenarios, new forms and new modes of digital tourism, and deep integration of digital economy and tourism real economy. This state-of-the-art review will help to reflect the efforts towards promoting the smart development of digital technologies in tourism.

hot.title: Service quality in mobile banking
hot.abstract: Purpose The rise of mobile technologies has driven rapid growth in mobile banking (m-banking), making service quality a central area of inquiry for researchers and industry practitioners alike. Despite this focus, understanding of service quality in m-banking remains fragmented. In this regard, this article endeavors to provide a comprehensive, state-of-the-art overview of service quality in m-banking. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on a systematic review of 71 studies, this article explores the concept of service quality in m-banking through the lens of theories, constructs, contexts, and methods (TCCM), revealing the multifaceted nature of service quality and its role in m-banking. Findings The review underscores the multifaceted nature of service quality and its pivotal role in steering pivotal customer-centric outcomes in m-banking. Introducing the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework into the discourse of m-banking, the review reveals a range of quality-, system success-, and user-based stimuli, affecting m-banking users’ attitude, brand attachment, flow, and trust, thus shaping their intended and actual behavior, including usage, satisfaction, loyalty, and word-of-mouth. Further scrutiny underscores opportunities for renewed endeavors to bridge identifiable gaps by harnessing mixed methods, exploring new constructs, probing demographic and cross-cultural variations, and forging new instruments tailored to evaluate contemporary m-banking service quality. Originality/value This review distinguishes itself by providing a comprehensive and systematic exploration of service quality in m-banking through the lens of TCCM. Unlike previous studies that often focus on isolated aspects, this review integrates diverse perspectives to offer a holistic understandin

hot.title: Guidelines for Theory Selection: The IMPACT Framework
hot.abstract: Though the role of adopting an appropriate theory in shaping the publishability and impact of research has long been recognized, psychology and marketing researchers lack specific guidance on how to choose a theory to frame their work. Addressing this gap in the literature, this article proposes a set of guidelines for the selection of relevant macro‐foundational theory to guide research projects addressing specific meso‐ or micro‐foundational theoretical entities (e.g., constructs or individual decision‐making) for research impact. Specifically, we develop a set of six guidelines to select an appropriate macro‐foundational theory for research impact, including Interestingness , Matching , Parsimony , Applicability , Conceptual rigor , and Testability (collectively abbreviated as the “IMPACT” guidelines). We next depict the proposed guidelines in an organizing framework that specifies Matching , the theoretical co ‐infusion of the studied micro‐ or meso‐foundational theoretical entity and the chosen macro‐foundational theory, as the central action item for researchers to shape the impact of their work. Researchers are then advised to use the five remaining guidelines to assess the quality of their proposed Matching for research impact. We conclude by discussing pertinent implications that arise from our analyses (e.g., to ensure Interestingness , we recommend researchers to select a macro‐foundational theory that refutes (vs. affirms) prior findings).

hot.title: The influence of brand experience on brand loyalty in the electronic commerce sector: the mediating effect of brand association and brand trust
hot.abstract: Businesses are increasingly focusing on brand experience due to its dual role in directly creating customer value and shaping customers’ perceptions of brand equity. This study investigates the impact of brand experience on brand equity in Vietnam’s e-commerce sector. Primary data were collected from respondents with prior online shopping experience on e-commerce platforms. The research identifies four critical dimensions of brand experience in e-commerce services: sensory, affective, intellectual, and behavioral experiences. These components positively influence brand equity, particularly in terms of brand association, brand trust, and brand loyalty. Moreover, the study confirms the mediating roles of brand association and brand trust in the relationships between affective experience and brand loyalty, intellectual experience and brand loyalty, and behavioral experience and brand loyalty. This research offers a valuable contribution to the literature on brand experience and brand equity, especially within the e-commerce context. Managerial implications are also provided to guide businesses in enhancing customer brand experiences and strengthening brand equity.

hot.title: Unveiling the future of responsible, sustainable, and ethical consumption: a bibliometric study on Gen Z and young consumers
hot.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
hot.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the key research themes and their evolutionary trajectory within the Gen Z and young consumers (GZYC) field, focusing on the interconnected dimensions of responsible, sustainable and ethical consumption. By using thematic maps and co-occurrence networks, the research seeks to identify significant trends and interconnections that shape sustainable behavior among this demographic. Design/methodology/approach This study used a bibliometric analysis of 546 papers sourced from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, following the framework established by Zupic and Cater (2015), Donthu (2024), Donthu et al. (2021) and Lim et al. (2024). Using R and Biblioshiny, the authors conducted performance analysis and science mapping to examine scientific output and conceptual themes within the GZYC field. Findings The performance analysis reveals an annual growth rate of 22.02% in publications, highlighting the increasing research interest in this area. The keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed eight distinct research clusters within the GZYC field, each representing key dimensions of responsible, sustainable and ethical consumption. These clusters encompass themes such as corporate social responsibility, gender and generational differences, green products, food sustainability, pro-environmental behaviors, the sharing economy and collaborative consumption, among others. The thematic maps and evolution revealed that over time, the focus has shifted.
